सर्वग्रहाणामेतेषामादिरादित्य उच्यते।
ताराग्रहाणां शुक्रस्तु केतूनाञ्चैव धूमवान् ॥ 53.111 ॥
1.53.m: The sun is said to be the beginning of all these planets; / Venus [the beginning] of the minor planets, and the smoky one of the comets.

1.53.s:
dhruvaḥ kālo grahāṇāṃ tu vibhaktānāṃ caturdiśam .
nakṣatrāṇāṃ śraviṣṭhā syādayanānāṃ tathottaram .. 53.112 ..
1.53.d:
ध्रुवः कालो ग्रहाणां तु विभक्तानां चतुर्दिशम् ।
नक्षत्राणां श्रविष्ठा स्यादयनानां तथोत्तरम् ॥ 53.112 ॥
1.53.m: Dhruva is the fixed time of the planets divided among the four quarters. / Śraviṣṭhā is [the first] of asterisms, and the northern is [the first] of solstices.

1.53.s:
varṣāṇāñcāpi pañcānāmādyaḥ saṃvatsaraḥ smṛtaḥ.
ṛtūnāṃ śiśirañcāpi māsānāṃ māgha eva ca .. 53.113 ..
1.53.d:
वर्षाणाञ्चापि पञ्चानामाद्यः संवत्सरः स्मृतः।
ऋतूनां शिशिरञ्चापि मासानां माघ एव च ॥ 53.113 ॥
1.53.m: Among the five years, Saṃvatsara is remembered as the first; / Śiśira is [the first] among seasons, and Māgha among months.

1.53.s:
pakṣāṇāṃ śuklapakṣastu tithīnāṃ pratipattathā.
ahorātravibhāgānāmahaścāpi prakīrtitam .. 53.114 ..
1.53.d:
पक्षाणां शुक्लपक्षस्तु तिथीनां प्रतिपत्तथा।
अहोरात्रविभागानामहश्चापि प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 53.114 ॥
1.53.m: The bright fortnight is [the first] of fortnights, and Pratipat of lunar days; / day is declared to be [the first] of the divisions of day and night.

1.53.s:
muhūrttānāṃ tathaivādirmuhūrtto rudradaivataḥ.
akṣṇoścāpi nimeṣādiḥ kālaḥ kālavido mataḥ .. 53.115 ..
1.53.d:
मुहूर्त्तानां तथैवादिर्मुहूर्त्तो रुद्रदैवतः।
अक्ष्णोश्चापि निमेषादिः कालः कालविदो मतः ॥ 53.115 ॥
1.53.m: So too, the muhūrta whose deity is Rudra is the beginning of muhūrtas. / The blinking of the eye and the rest are considered by knowers of time to be the beginning of time.

1.53.s:
śravaṇāntaṃ śraviṣṭhādiyugaṃ syāt pañcavārṣikam.
bhānorgativiśeṣeṇa cakravat parivarttate .. 53.116 ..
1.53.d:
श्रवणान्तं श्रविष्ठादियुगं स्यात् पञ्चवार्षिकम्।
भानोर्गतिविशेषेण चक्रवत् परिवर्त्तते ॥ 53.116 ॥
1.53.m: The five-year yuga begins with Śraviṣṭhā and ends with Śravaṇa. / Through the specific motion of the sun, it revolves like a wheel.

1.53.s:
divākaraḥ smṛtastasmātkālastaṃ viddhi ceśvaram.
caturvanidhānāṃ bhūtānāṃ pravarttakanivarttakaḥ .. 53.117 ..
1.53.d:
दिवाकरः स्मृतस्तस्मात्कालस्तं विद्धि चेश्वरम्।
चतुर्वनिधानां भूतानां प्रवर्त्तकनिवर्त्तकः ॥ 53.117 ॥
1.53.m: Therefore the sun is remembered as time; know him to be the lord, / the impeller and withdrawer of the four kinds of living beings.

1.53.s:
ityeṣa jyotiṣāmeva sanniveśo'rthaniścayāt.
lokasaṃvyavahārārthamīśvareṇa vinirmitaḥ .. 53.118 ..
1.53.d:
इत्येष ज्योतिषामेव सन्निवेशोऽर्थनिश्चयात्।
लोकसंव्यवहारार्थमीश्वरेण विनिर्मितः ॥ 53.118 ॥
1.53.m: Thus this arrangement of the heavenly bodies, according to the ascertainment of the matter, / was fashioned by the Lord for the sake of worldly convention.

1.53.s:
utpannaḥ śravaṇenāsau saṃkṣiptaśca dhruve tathā.
sarvato'nteṣu vistīrṇo vṛkṣākāra iti sthitiḥ .. 53.119 ..
1.53.d:
उत्पन्नः श्रवणेनासौ संक्षिप्तश्च ध्रुवे तथा।
सर्वतोऽन्तेषु विस्तीर्णो वृक्षाकार इति स्थितिः ॥ 53.119 ॥
1.53.m: Arisen with Śravaṇa and contracted at Dhruva, / extended all around at the ends, its standing form is shaped like a tree.

1.53.s:
buddhipūrvambhagavatā kalpādau saṃprakīrtitaḥ.
sāśrayaḥ so'bhimānī ca sarvasya jyotirātmakaḥ.
viśvarūpaḥ pradhānasya pariṇāmo'yamadbhutaḥ .. 53.120 ..
1.53.d:
बुद्धिपूर्वम्भगवता कल्पादौ संप्रकीर्तितः।
साश्रयः सोऽभिमानी च सर्वस्य ज्योतिरात्मकः।
विश्वरूपः प्रधानस्य परिणामोऽयमद्भुतः ॥ 53.120 ॥
1.53.m: It was declared purposefully by the Lord at the beginning of the aeon. / Possessing a support, endowed with self-consciousness, made of light, / multiform, this wondrous transformation belongs to Pradhāna.

1.53.s:
naiva śakyaṃ prasaṃkhyātuṃ yāthātathyena kenacit.
gatāgataṃ manuṣyeṣu jyotiṣāṃ māṃsacakṣuṣā .. 53.121 ..
1.53.d:
नैव शक्यं प्रसंख्यातुं याथातथ्येन केनचित्।
गतागतं मनुष्येषु ज्योतिषां मांसचक्षुषा ॥ 53.121 ॥
1.53.m: It is not possible for anyone among men with the eye of flesh / to calculate truly the coming and going of the heavenly bodies.

1.53.s:
āgamādanumānācca pratyakṣādupapattitaḥ.
parīkṣya nipuṇaṃ bhaktyā śraddhātavyaṃ vipaścitā .. 53.122 ..
1.53.d:
आगमादनुमानाच्च प्रत्यक्षादुपपत्तितः।
परीक्ष्य निपुणं भक्त्या श्रद्धातव्यं विपश्चिता ॥ 53.122 ॥
1.53.m: Having examined carefully through sacred tradition, inference, / direct perception, and logical proof, the wise man must have faith with devotion.

1.53.s:
cakṣuḥ śāstraṃ jalaṃ lekhyaṃ gaṇitaṃ buddhisattamāḥ.
pañcaite hetavo jñeyā jyotirgaṇavicintane .. 53.123 ..
1.53.d:
चक्षुः शास्त्रं जलं लेख्यं गणितं बुद्धिसत्तमाः।
पञ्चैते हेतवो ज्ञेया ज्योतिर्गणविचिन्तने ॥ 53.123 ॥
1.53.m: The eye, scripture, water, drawing, and calculation, O best of the wise: / these five are to be known as the means in contemplating the assembly of heavenly bodies.

1.53.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte jyotiḥsanniveśo nāma tripañcāśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 53 ...
1.53.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते ज्योतिःसन्निवेशो नाम त्रिपञ्चाशोऽध्यायः ॥ 53 ॥।
1.53.m: Thus ends the fifty-third chapter, named 'The Arrangement of Heavenly Bodies', in the holy Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.54.s: ..ṛṣaya ūcuḥ..
1.54.d: ॥ऋषय ऊचुः॥
1.54.m:
The seers said:
In which country and at what time, O greatly radiant one,
did this most sacred, excellent narrative of those headed by Brahmā take place?
Tell this to us properly as it happened, O you whose wealth is asceticism.

1.54.s:
kasmin deśe mahāpuṇyametadākhyānamuttamam.
vṛttaṃ brahmapurogāṇāṃ kasmin kāle mahādyute.
etadākhyāhi naḥ samyag yathā vṛttaṃ tapodhana .. 54.1 ..
1.54.d:
कस्मिन् देशे महापुण्यमेतदाख्यानमुत्तमम्।
वृत्तं ब्रह्मपुरोगाणां कस्मिन् काले महाद्युते।
एतदाख्याहि नः सम्यग् यथा वृत्तं तपोधन ॥ 54.1 ॥

1.54.s: ..sūta uvāca..
1.54.d: ॥सूत उवाच॥
1.54.m:
The Sūta said:
O best of the twice-born, hear how it was heard by me formerly,
as it was being narrated by Vāyu, the life of the world, at a thousand-year sacrificial session.

1.54.s:
yathā śrutaṃ mayā pūrvaṃ vāyunā jagadāyunā.
kathyamānaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ satre varṣasahasrake .. 54.2 ..
1.54.d:
यथा श्रुतं मया पूर्वं वायुना जगदायुना।
कथ्यमानं द्विजश्रेष्ठाः सत्रे वर्षसहस्रके ॥ 54.2 ॥

1.54.s:
nīlatā yena kaṇṭhasya devadevasya śūlinaḥ.
tadahaṃ kīrttayiṣyāmi śrṛṇudhvaṃ śaṃsitavratāḥ .. 54.3 ..
1.54.d:
नीलता येन कण्ठस्य देवदेवस्य शूलिनः।
तदहं कीर्त्तयिष्यामि श्रृणुध्वं शंसितव्रताः ॥ 54.3 ॥
1.54.m: by which the throat of the spear-bearing god of gods became black, / that I shall recount; listen, O you of confirmed vows!

1.54.s:
uttare śailarājasya sarāṃsi sarito hradāḥ.
puṇyodyāneṣu tīrtheṣu devatāyataneṣu ca.
giriśrṛṅgeṣu tuṅgeṣu gahvaropavaneṣu ca .. 54.4 ..
1.54.d:
उत्तरे शैलराजस्य सरांसि सरितो ह्रदाः।
पुण्योद्यानेषु तीर्थेषु देवतायतनेषु च।
गिरिश्रृङ्गेषु तुङ्गेषु गह्वरोपवनेषु च ॥ 54.4 ॥
1.54.m: To the north of the king of mountains are lakes, rivers, pools, / in holy gardens, holy bathing places, and temples of deities, / on lofty mountain peaks and in cavern groves,

1.54.s:
devabhaktā mahātmāno munayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ.
stuvanti ca mahādevaṃ yatra yathāvidhi .. 54.5 ..
1.54.d:
देवभक्ता महात्मानो मुनयः शंसितव्रताः।
स्तुवन्ति च महादेवं यत्र यथाविधि ॥ 54.5 ॥
1.54.m: where the high-souled sages, devoted to the gods and of confirmed vows, / praise Mahādeva according to rule,

1.54.s:
ṛgyajuḥsāmavedaiśca nṛtyagītārccanādibhiḥ.
oṅkāreṇa namaskārairarccayanti sadā śivam .. 54.6 ..
1.54.d:
ऋग्यजुःसामवेदैश्च नृत्यगीतार्च्चनादिभिः।
ओङ्कारेण नमस्कारैरर्च्चयन्ति सदा शिवम् ॥ 54.6 ॥
1.54.m: and with the Rig-, Yajur-, and Sāmavedas, with dances, songs, and worship, / with the syllable Oṃ and with prostrations, they ever worship Śiva.

1.54.s:
pravṛtte jyotiṣāṃ cakre madhyavyāpte divākare.
devatā niyatātmānaḥ sarve tiṣṭhanti tāṃ kathām .
atha niyamapravṛttāśca prāṇaśeṣavyavasthitāḥ .. 54.7 ..
1.54.d:
प्रवृत्ते ज्योतिषां चक्रे मध्यव्याप्ते दिवाकरे।
देवता नियतात्मानः सर्वे तिष्ठन्ति तां कथाम् ।
अथ नियमप्रवृत्ताश्च प्राणशेषव्यवस्थिताः ॥ 54.7 ॥
1.54.m: When the wheel of the heavenly bodies has turned and the sun covers the middle, / the deities, self-restrained, all wait for that story. / Then, engaged in restrictions, they remain with only their life-breath left."

1.54.s:
namaste nīlakaṇṭhāya ityuvāca sadāgatiḥ.
tacchutvā bhāvitātmāno munayaḥ śaṃśitavratāḥ.
vālakhilyeti vikhyātāḥ pataṅgasahacāriṇaḥ .. 54.8 ..
1.54.d:
नमस्ते नीलकण्ठाय इत्युवाच सदागतिः।
तच्छुत्वा भावितात्मानो मुनयः शंशितव्रताः।
वालखिल्येति विख्याताः पतङ्गसहचारिणः ॥ 54.8 ॥
1.54.m: "Homage to you, the blue-throated one!" so said Sadāgati. / Hearing that, the sages of cultured minds, strict in vows, / famed as the Vālakhilyas, companions of the sun,

1.54.s:
aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi munīnāmūrddhvaretasām.
tasmāt pṛcchanti vai vāyuṃ vāyuparṇāmbubhojanāḥ .. 54.9 ..
1.54.d:
अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि मुनीनामूर्द्ध्वरेतसाम्।
तस्मात् पृच्छन्ति वै वायुं वायुपर्णाम्बुभोजनाः ॥ 54.9 ॥
1.54.m: eighty-eight thousand sages of upward-drawn seed, / living on air, fallen leaves, and water, questioned Vāyu:

1.54.s: ..ṛṣaya ūcuḥ..
1.54.d: ॥ऋषय ऊचुः॥
1.54.m:
The seers said:
That you addressed [him] as Nīlakaṇṭha, O best of winds,
is a secret among purifiers, holy, O best among performers of holy deeds.

1.54.s:
nīlakaṇṭheti yat proktaṃ tvayā pavanasattama.
etadduhyaṃ pavitrāṇāṃ puṇyaṃ puṇyakṛtāṃ varāḥ .. 54.10 ..
1.54.d:
नीलकण्ठेति यत् प्रोक्तं त्वया पवनसत्तम।
एतद्दुह्यं पवित्राणां पुण्यं पुण्यकृतां वराः ॥ 54.10 ॥

1.54.s:
tadvayaṃ śrotumicchāmastvatprasādātprabhañjana.
nīlatā yena kaṇṭhasya kāraṇenāmbikāpateḥ .. 54.11 ..
1.54.d:
तद्वयं श्रोतुमिच्छामस्त्वत्प्रसादात्प्रभञ्जन।
नीलता येन कण्ठस्य कारणेनाम्बिकापतेः ॥ 54.11 ॥
1.54.m: We wish to hear that through your grace, O Prabhañcana— / the reason by which the throat of the lord of Ambikā became blue.

1.54.s:
śrotumicchā mahe samyak tava vakrādviśeṣataḥ.
yāvadvācaḥ pravarttante sārthāstāśca tvayeritāḥ .. 54.12 ..
1.54.d:
श्रोतुमिच्छा महे सम्यक् तव वक्राद्विशेषतः।
यावद्वाचः प्रवर्त्तन्ते सार्थास्ताश्च त्वयेरिताः ॥ 54.12 ॥
1.54.m: We wish to hear it properly, especially from your mouth, / for as long as words proceed endowed with meaning, they are prompted by you.

1.54.s:
varṇasthānagate vāyau vāgvidhiḥ saṃpravartate.
jñānaṃ pūrvamathotsāha stvatto vāyo pravartate .. 54.13 .
tvayi niṣpandamāne tu śeṣā varṇapravṛttayaḥ.
yatra vāco nivartante dehabandhāśca durlabhāḥ .. 54.14 ..
1.54.d:
वर्णस्थानगते वायौ वाग्विधिः संप्रवर्तते।
ज्ञानं पूर्वमथोत्साह स्त्वत्तो वायो प्रवर्तते ॥ 54.13 ।
त्वयि निष्पन्दमाने तु शेषा वर्णप्रवृत्तयः।
यत्र वाचो निवर्तन्ते देहबन्धाश्च दुर्लभाः ॥ 54.14 ॥
1.54.m: When the wind reaches the vocal positions, speech is produced; / knowledge comes first, then enthusiasm arises from you, O Vāyu. / But when you become motionless, the rest of the sound operations [cease]; / where speech turns back, and bodily bonds are hard to attain,

1.54.s:
tatrāpi te'sti sadbhāvaḥ sarvagastvaṃ sadānila.
nānyaḥ sarvagato devastvadṛteśa़sti samīraṇa .. 54.15 ..
1.54.d:
तत्रापि तेऽस्ति सद्भावः सर्वगस्त्वं सदानिल।
नान्यः सर्वगतो देवस्त्वदृतेश़स्ति समीरण ॥ 54.15 ॥
1.54.m: even there your real existence remains, for you are all-pervading, O eternal wind! / There is no other all-pervading god besides you, O wind!

1.54.s:
eṣa vai jīvalokaste pratyakṣaḥ sarvato'nila.
vettha vācaspatiṃ devaṃ manonāyakamīsvaram .. 54.16 ..
1.54.d:
एष वै जीवलोकस्ते प्रत्यक्षः सर्वतोऽनिल।
वेत्थ वाचस्पतिं देवं मनोनायकमीस्वरम् ॥ 54.16 ॥
1.54.m: This world of living beings is directly perceived by you everywhere, O wind. / You know the lord of speech, the god, the ruler who guides the mind.

1.54.s:
brūhi tatkaṇṭhadeśasya kiṃ kṛtā rūpavikriyā.
śrutvā vākyantatasteṣāmṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmānām.
pratyuvāca mahātejā vāyurloka namaskṛtaḥ .. 54.17 ..
1.54.d:
ब्रूहि तत्कण्ठदेशस्य किं कृता रूपविक्रिया।
श्रुत्वा वाक्यन्ततस्तेषामृषीणां भावितात्मानाम्।
प्रत्युवाच महातेजा वायुर्लोक नमस्कृतः ॥ 54.17 ॥
1.54.m: Tell us: why was this alteration in appearance made to his throat region?" / Hearing that speech of those seers of cultured minds, / Vāyu, possessing great splendour and worshipped by the world, replied:

1.54.s: ..vāyuruvāca..
1.54.d: ॥वायुरुवाच॥
1.54.m:
Vāyu said:
Formerly, in the Kṛtayuga, there was a brāhmaṇa intent on ascertaining the Veda,
named Vasiṣṭha, righteous, the mind-born [son] of Prajāpati.

1.54.s:
purā kṛtayuge vipro vedanirṇayatatparaḥ.
vasiṣṭho nāma dharmātmā mānaso vai prajāpateḥ .. 54.18 ..
1.54.d:
पुरा कृतयुगे विप्रो वेदनिर्णयतत्परः।
वसिष्ठो नाम धर्मात्मा मानसो वै प्रजापतेः ॥ 54.18 ॥

1.54.s:
prapaccha kārtikeyaṃ vai mayūravaravāhanam.
mahiṣāsuranārīṇāṃ nayanāñjanataskaram .. 54.19 ..
1.54.d:
प्रपच्छ कार्तिकेयं वै मयूरवरवाहनम्।
महिषासुरनारीणां नयनाञ्जनतस्करम् ॥ 54.19 ॥
1.54.m: inquired of Kārtikeya, whose mount is the excellent peacock, / who stole the eye-collyrium of the women of Mahiṣāsura,

1.54.s:
mahāsenaṃ mahātmānaṃ meghastanitaniḥsvanam.
umāmanaḥpraharṣeṇa bālakaṃ chajharūpiṇam .. 54.20 ..
1.54.d:
महासेनं महात्मानं मेघस्तनितनिःस्वनम्।
उमामनःप्रहर्षेण बालकं छझरूपिणम् ॥ 54.20 ॥
1.54.m: Mahāsena, the great-souled one, whose voice is like the rumbling of a cloud, / who, as a child, delighted the mind of Umā, appearing in disguise,

1.54.s:
krauñcajīvitaharttāraṃ pārvatīhṛdi nandanam.
vasiṣṭhaḥ pṛcchate bhaktyā kārtikeyaṃ mahābalam .. 54.21 ..
1.54.d:
क्रौञ्चजीवितहर्त्तारं पार्वतीहृदि नन्दनम्।
वसिष्ठः पृच्छते भक्त्या कार्तिकेयं महाबलम् ॥ 54.21 ॥
1.54.m: who took the life of Krauñca, the delighter of Pārvatī's heart— / Vasiṣṭha asked the mighty Kārtikeya with devotion:

1.54.s: ..vasiṣṭha uvāca..
1.54.d: ॥वसिष्ठ उवाच॥
1.54.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
Homage to you, the joy of Hara! Homage be to you, the child of Umā's womb!
Homage to you, child of Agni's womb! Homage be to you, child of Gaṅgā's womb!

1.54.s:
namaste haranandāya umāgarbha namo 'stu te.
namaste agnigarbhāya gaṅgāgarbha namo'stu te .. 54.22 ..
1.54.d:
नमस्ते हरनन्दाय उमागर्भ नमो ऽस्तु ते।
नमस्ते अग्निगर्भाय गङ्गागर्भ नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 54.22 ॥

1.54.s:
namaste śaragarbhāya namaste kṛttikāsuta.
namo dvādaśanetrāya ṣaṇmukhāya namo'stu te .. 54.23 ..
1.54.d:
नमस्ते शरगर्भाय नमस्ते कृत्तिकासुत।
नमो द्वादशनेत्राय षण्मुखाय नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 54.23 ॥
1.54.m: "Homage to you, born in the reed clump! Homage to you, son of the Kṛttikās! / Homage to the twelve-eyed one! Homage be to the six-faced one!

1.54.s:
namaste śaktihastāya divyaghaṇṭāpatākine.
evaṃ stutvā mahāsenaṃ papraccha śikhivāhanam .. 54.24 ..
1.54.d:
नमस्ते शक्तिहस्ताय दिव्यघण्टापताकिने।
एवं स्तुत्वा महासेनं पप्रच्छ शिखिवाहनम् ॥ 54.24 ॥
1.54.m: "Homage to you with a spear in hand, having divine bells and banners!" / Having praised Mahāsena thus, he questioned the one whose mount is the peacock:

1.54.s:
yadetaddṛśyate varṇaṃ śubhaṃ śubhrāñjanaprabham.
tatkimarthaṃ samutpannaṃ kaṇṭhe kundendusaṃprabhe .. 54.25 ..
1.54.d:
यदेतद्दृश्यते वर्णं शुभं शुभ्राञ्जनप्रभम्।
तत्किमर्थं समुत्पन्नं कण्ठे कुन्देन्दुसंप्रभे ॥ 54.25 ॥
1.54.m: "This bright colour that is seen, radiant like pure black collyrium— / for what purpose did it arise on the throat that shines like jasmine and the moon?

1.54.s:
etadāptāya bhaktāya dāntāya brūhi pṛcchate.
kathāṃ maṅgalasaṃyuktāṃ pavitrāṃ pāpanāśinīm .
matpriyārthaṃ mahābhāga vaktumarhasyaśeṣataḥ .. 54.26 ..
1.54.d:
एतदाप्ताय भक्ताय दान्ताय ब्रूहि पृच्छते।
कथां मङ्गलसंयुक्तां पवित्रां पापनाशिनीम् ।
मत्प्रियार्थं महाभाग वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः ॥ 54.26 ॥
1.54.m: "Speak of this to a trusted devotee, restrained, who asks you; / you should tell in full, O illustrious one, for my satisfaction, / the auspicious, purifying narrative that destroys sins."

1.54.s:
śrutvā vākyaṃ tatastasya vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ.
pratyuvāca mahātejāḥ surāribalasūdanaḥ .. 54.27 ..
1.54.d:
श्रुत्वा वाक्यं ततस्तस्य वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः।
प्रत्युवाच महातेजाः सुरारिबलसूदनः ॥ 54.27 ॥
1.54.m: Hearing that speech of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, / the highly splendid slayer of the army of the enemies of the gods replied:

1.54.s:
śrṛṇuṣva vadatāṃ śreṣṭha kathyamānaṃ vaco mama.
umotsaṅganiviṣṭena mayā pūrvaṃ yathāśrutam .. 54.28 ..
1.54.d:
श्रृणुष्व वदतां श्रेष्ठ कथ्यमानं वचो मम।
उमोत्सङ्गनिविष्टेन मया पूर्वं यथाश्रुतम् ॥ 54.28 ॥
1.54.m: "Listen, O best of speakers, to my words being spoken, / just as I heard them long ago while seated in the lap of Umā.

1.54.s:
pārvatyā saha saṃvādaḥ śarvasya ca mahātmanaḥ.
tadahaṅkīrttayiṣyāmi tvatpriyārthaṃ mahāmune .. 54.29 ..
1.54.d:
पार्वत्या सह संवादः शर्वस्य च महात्मनः।
तदहङ्कीर्त्तयिष्यामि त्वत्प्रियार्थं महामुने ॥ 54.29 ॥
1.54.m: The conversation between Pārvatī and the great-souled Śarva— / that I shall recount for your satisfaction, O great seer.

1.54.s:
kailāsaśikhare ramye nānādhātuvicitrite.
nānādrumalatākīrṇe cakravākopaśobhite .. 54.30 ..
1.54.d:
कैलासशिखरे रम्ये नानाधातुविचित्रिते।
नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णे चक्रवाकोपशोभिते ॥ 54.30 ॥
1.54.m: On the charming peak of Kailāsa, variegated with diverse minerals, / crowded with diverse trees and creepers, adorned with ruddy shelducks,

1.54.s:
ṣaṭ‌padodgītabahule dhārāsampātanādite.
mattakrauñcamayūrāṇāṃ nādairudghuṣṭakandare .. 54.31 ..
1.54.d:
षट्‌पदोद्गीतबहुले धारासम्पातनादिते।
मत्तक्रौञ्चमयूराणां नादैरुद्घुष्टकन्दरे ॥ 54.31 ॥
1.54.m: abounding in the buzzing songs of bees, resounding with the fall of cascades, / its caves echoing with the cries of impassioned curlews and peacocks,

1.54.s:
apsarogaṇasaṅkīrṇe kinnaraiścopaśobhite .
jīvañjīvakajātīnāṃ vīrudbhirupaśobhite .. 54.32 ..
1.54.d:
अप्सरोगणसङ्कीर्णे किन्नरैश्चोपशोभिते ।
जीवञ्जीवकजातीनां वीरुद्भिरुपशोभिते ॥ 54.32 ॥
1.54.m: thronged with hosts of apsarases and adorned by kinnaras, / adorned by shoots and flocks of partridges,

1.54.s:
kokilārāvamadhure siddha cāraṇasevite.
saurabhaiyīninādāḍhye adhastanitaniḥsvane .. 54.33 ..
1.54.d:
कोकिलारावमधुरे सिद्ध चारणसेविते।
सौरभैयीनिनादाढ्ये अधस्तनितनिःस्वने ॥ 54.33 ॥
1.54.m: sweet with the cooing of cuckoos, frequented by siddhas and cāraṇas, / rich with the sounds of celestial cows, with deep reverberating noises below,

1.54.s:
vināyakabhayodvigne kuñjarairyuktakandare.
vīṇāvāditranirghoṣaiḥ śrotrendriyamanoramaiḥ .. 54.34 ..
1.54.d:
विनायकभयोद्विग्ने कुञ्जरैर्युक्तकन्दरे।
वीणावादित्रनिर्घोषैः श्रोत्रेन्द्रियमनोरमैः ॥ 54.34 ॥
1.54.m: its caves filled with elephants frightened in fear of Vināyaka, / with the sounds of lutes and musical instruments delightful to the ear,

1.54.s:
dolālambitasampāte vanitāsaṅghasevite.
dhvajairlambitadolānāṃ ghaṇṭhānāṃ ninadākule .. 54.35 ..
1.54.d:
दोलालम्बितसम्पाते वनितासङ्घसेविते।
ध्वजैर्लम्बितदोलानां घण्ठानां निनदाकुले ॥ 54.35 ॥
1.54.m: swaying on hanging swings, frequented by groups of women, / crowded with the ringing of bells on swings adorned with banners,

1.54.s:
mukhamardalavāditrairbalināṃ sphoṭitaistathā.
krīḍāravavicārāṇāṃ nirghoṣaiḥ pūrṇamandire .. 54.36 ..
1.54.d:
मुखमर्दलवादित्रैर्बलिनां स्फोटितैस्तथा।
क्रीडारवविचाराणां निर्घोषैः पूर्णमन्दिरे ॥ 54.36 ॥
1.54.m: with face-drums and instruments, and clapping by the strong, / its dwelling filled with the sounds of playful wanderings,

1.54.s:
hāsaiḥ santrāsajananairvikarālamukhaistathā.
dehagandhairvicitraiśca prakrīḍitagaṇeścaraiḥ .. 54.37 ..
1.54.d:
हासैः सन्त्रासजननैर्विकरालमुखैस्तथा।
देहगन्धैर्विचित्रैश्च प्रक्रीडितगणेश्चरैः ॥ 54.37 ॥
1.54.m: with terrifyng bursts of laughter and ferocious faces, / and diverse bodily scents, with lords of gaṇas sporting about,

1.54.s:
vajrasphaṭikasopāna citrapaṭṭiśilātalaiḥ.
vyādhrasiṃhamukhaiśacavānyairgajavājimukhaistathā .. 54.38 ..
1.54.d:
वज्रस्फटिकसोपान चित्रपट्टिशिलातलैः।
व्याध्रसिंहमुखैशचवान्यैर्गजवाजिमुखैस्तथा ॥ 54.38 ॥
1.54.m: with steps of diamond and crystal, and floors of variegated stone slabs, / [beings] with faces of tigers and lions, and others with faces of elephants and horses,

1.54.s:
biḍālavadanaiścograiḥ kroṣṭukākāramūrtibhiḥ .
hrasvairdīrghaiḥ kṛśaiḥ sthūlairlambodara mahodaraiḥ .. 54.39 ..
1.54.d:
बिडालवदनैश्चोग्रैः क्रोष्टुकाकारमूर्तिभिः ।
ह्रस्वैर्दीर्घैः कृशैः स्थूलैर्लम्बोदर महोदरैः ॥ 54.39 ॥
1.54.m: with cat faces and terrifying, having the forms of jackals, / short, tall, thin, stout, with hanging bellies and large bellies,

1.54.s:
hrasvajaṅghaiśca lamboṣṭhaistālajaṅghaistathāparaiḥ.
gaukarṇairekakarṇaiśca mahākarṇairakarṇakaiḥ .. 54.40 ..
1.54.d:
ह्रस्वजङ्घैश्च लम्बोष्ठैस्तालजङ्घैस्तथापरैः।
गौकर्णैरेककर्णैश्च महाकर्णैरकर्णकैः ॥ 54.40 ॥
1.54.m: with short shanks and hanging lips, and others with shanks like palm trees, / with cow-ears, single-eared, huge-eared, and earless,

1.54.s:
bahupādairmahāpādairekapādairapādakaiḥ.
bahuśīrṣairmahāśīrṣairekaśīrṣairaśīrṣakaiḥ .. 54.41 ..
1.54.d:
बहुपादैर्महापादैरेकपादैरपादकैः।
बहुशीर्षैर्महाशीर्षैरेकशीर्षैरशीर्षकैः ॥ 54.41 ॥
1.54.m: many-footed, huge-footed, one-footed, and footless, / many-headed, huge-headed, one-headed, and headless,

1.54.s:
bahunetrairmahānetrairekanaitrairanaitrakaiḥ .
evaṃvidhairmahāyogibhūtairbhūtapatirvṛtaḥ .. 54.42 ..
1.54.d:
बहुनेत्रैर्महानेत्रैरेकनैत्रैरनैत्रकैः ।
एवंविधैर्महायोगिभूतैर्भूतपतिर्वृतः ॥ 54.42 ॥
1.54.m: many-eyed, huge-eyed, one-eyed, and eyeless— / surrounded by such great yogic spirits, the lord of spirits,

1.54.s:
viśuddhamuktāmaṇiratnabhūṣite śilātale hemamaye manorame.
sukhopaviṣṭaṃ madanāṅganāśanaṃ provāca vākyaṃ girirājaputrī .. 54.43 ..
1.54.d:
विशुद्धमुक्तामणिरत्नभूषिते शिलातले हेममये मनोरमे।
सुखोपविष्टं मदनाङ्गनाशनं प्रोवाच वाक्यं गिरिराजपुत्री ॥ 54.43 ॥
1.54.m: seated comfortably on a charming golden stone slab decorated with pure pearls and gems, / the daughter of the king of mountains addressed the destroyer of the body of Kama:

1.54.s: ..devyuvāca..
1.54.d: ॥देव्युवाच॥
1.54.m:
The goddess said:
O blessed one, ruler of what has been and what is to be, whose decree is marked with a bull,
[what is this that] shines upon your throat, O Mahādeva, resembling a rain cloud?

1.54.s:
bhagavan bhūtabhavyeśa govṛṣāṅkitaśāsana.
tava kaṇṭhe mahādeva bhrājate'mbudaśannibham .. 54.44 ..
1.54.d:
भगवन् भूतभव्येश गोवृषाङ्कितशासन।
तव कण्ठे महादेव भ्राजतेऽम्बुदशन्निभम् ॥ 54.44 ॥

1.54.s:
nātyulbaṇaṃ nātiśubraṃ nīlāñjanacayopamam.
kimidaṃ dīpyate deva kaṇṭhe kāmāṅga nāśana .. 54.45 ..
1.54.d:
नात्युल्बणं नातिशुब्रं नीलाञ्जनचयोपमम्।
किमिदं दीप्यते देव कण्ठे कामाङ्ग नाशन ॥ 54.45 ॥
1.54.m: neither very dark nor very white, like a heap of blue collyrium. / What is this that gleams on your throat, O destroyer of the body of Desire?

1.54.s:
ko hetuḥ kāraṇaṃ kiñca kaṇṭhe nīlatvamīśvaraḥ .
etatsarvaṃ yathānyāyaṃ brūhi kautūhalaṃ hime .. 54.46 ..
1.54.d:
को हेतुः कारणं किञ्च कण्ठे नीलत्वमीश्वरः ।
एतत्सर्वं यथान्यायं ब्रूहि कौतूहलं हिमे ॥ 54.46 ॥
1.54.m: "What is the cause and what is the reason for the blueness on the throat, O Lord? / Tell me all this properly, for great curiosity has arisen in me."

1.54.s:
śrutvā vākyaṃ tatastasyāḥ pārvatyāḥ pārvatīpriyaḥ .
kathāṃ maṅgalasaṃyuktāṃ kathayāmāsa śaṅkaraḥ .. 54.47 ..
1.54.d:
श्रुत्वा वाक्यं ततस्तस्याः पार्वत्याः पार्वतीप्रियः ।
कथां मङ्गलसंयुक्तां कथयामास शङ्करः ॥ 54.47 ॥
1.54.m: Hearing that speech of hers, Śaṅkara, the beloved of Pārvatī, / recounted an auspicious tale to Pārvatī:

1.54.s:
mathyamāne'mṛte pūrvaṃ kṣīrode suradānavaiḥ.
agre samutthitaṃ tasmin viṣaṃ kālānalaprabham .. 54.48 ..
1.54.d:
मथ्यमानेऽमृते पूर्वं क्षीरोदे सुरदानवैः।
अग्रे समुत्थितं तस्मिन् विषं कालानलप्रभम् ॥ 54.48 ॥
1.54.m: "Long ago, when the nectar was being churned from the ocean of milk by gods and dānavas, / first there arose in it a poison radiant like the fire of destruction.

1.54.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā surasaṅghāśca daityāścaiva varānane.
viṣaṇṇavadanāḥ sarve gatāste brahmaṇo'ntikam .. 54.49 ..
1.54.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा सुरसङ्घाश्च दैत्याश्चैव वरानने।
विषण्णवदनाः सर्वे गतास्ते ब्रह्मणोऽन्तिकम् ॥ 54.49 ॥
1.54.m: Seeing that, the hosts of gods and the daityas, O fair-faced one, / all with dejected faces, went into the presence of Brahmā.

1.54.s:
dṛṣṭvā suragaṇān bhītān brahmo vāca mahādyutiḥ.
kimarthaṃ bho mahābhāgā bhītā udvignacetasaḥ .. 54.50 ..
1.54.d:
दृष्ट्वा सुरगणान् भीतान् ब्रह्मो वाच महाद्युतिः।
किमर्थं भो महाभागा भीता उद्विग्नचेतसः ॥ 54.50 ॥
1.54.m: Seeing the hosts of gods terrified, Brahmā of great splendour said: / “Why, O fortunate ones, are you terrified, your minds agitated?

1.54.s:
mayāṣṭaguṇamaiśvaryaṃ bhavatāṃ samprakalpitam.
kena vyāvarttitaiśvaryā yūyaṃ vai surasattamāḥ .. 54.51 ..
1.54.d:
मयाष्टगुणमैश्वर्यं भवतां सम्प्रकल्पितम्।
केन व्यावर्त्तितैश्वर्या यूयं वै सुरसत्तमाः ॥ 54.51 ॥
1.54.m: Eightfold sovereign power was established by me for you. / By whom has the sovereign power of you, the best of gods, been overturned?

1.54.s:
trailokyasyeśvarā yūyaṃ sarve vai vigatajvarāḥ.
prajāsarge na so'stīha ājñāṃ yo me nivarttayet .. 54.52 ..
1.54.d:
त्रैलोक्यस्येश्वरा यूयं सर्वे वै विगतज्वराः।
प्रजासर्गे न सोऽस्तीह आज्ञां यो मे निवर्त्तयेत् ॥ 54.52 ॥
1.54.m: You are the lords of the three worlds, all free from anguish. / In the creation of creatures there is no one here who would overturn my command.

1.54.s:
vimānagāminaḥ sarve sarve svacchandagāminaḥ.
adhyātme cādhibhūte ca adhidaive ca nityaśaḥ.
prajāḥ karmavipākena śaktā yūyaṃ pravarttitum .. 54.53 ..
1.54.d:
विमानगामिनः सर्वे सर्वे स्वच्छन्दगामिनः।
अध्यात्मे चाधिभूते च अधिदैवे च नित्यशः।
प्रजाः कर्मविपाकेन शक्ता यूयं प्रवर्त्तितुम् ॥ 54.53 ॥
1.54.m: All travelling in aerial chariots, all moving at will, / always in the spiritual, the elemental, and the divine spheres, / you are able to direct creatures according to the ripening of their deeds.

1.54.s:
tatkimarthaṃ bhayodvignā mṛgāḥ siṃhārditā iva.
kiṃ duḥkhaṃ kena santāpaḥ kulo vā bhayamāgatam.
etatsarvaṃ yathānyāyaṃ śīgramākhyātumarhatha .. 54.54 ..
1.54.d:
तत्किमर्थं भयोद्विग्ना मृगाः सिंहार्दिता इव।
किं दुःखं केन सन्तापः कुलो वा भयमागतम्।
एतत्सर्वं यथान्यायं शीग्रमाख्यातुमर्हथ ॥ 54.54 ॥
1.54.m: Then why are you distressed with fear, like deer harassed by a lion? / What is the sorrow? From what has torment come? Whence has fear arrived? / You ought to recount all this to me quickly and properly.”

1.54.s:
śrutvā vākyaṃ tatastasya brahmaṇo vai mahātmanaḥ.
ūcuste ṛṣibhiḥ sārdhdhaṃ suradaityendradānavāḥ .. 54.55 ..
1.54.d:
श्रुत्वा वाक्यं ततस्तस्य ब्रह्मणो वै महात्मनः।
ऊचुस्ते ऋषिभिः सार्ध्धं सुरदैत्येन्द्रदानवाः ॥ 54.55 ॥
1.54.m: Hearing that speech of that great-souled Brahmā, / those gods, chiefs of daityas, and dānavas spoke together with the seers:

1.54.s:
surāsurairmathyamāne pāthodhau ca mahātmabhiḥ.
bhujaṅgabhṛṅgasaṅkāśaṃ nīlajīmūtasannibham.
prādurbhūtaṃ viṣaṃ ghoraṃ saṃvartāgnisamaprabham .. 54.56 ..
1.54.d:
सुरासुरैर्मथ्यमाने पाथोधौ च महात्मभिः।
भुजङ्गभृङ्गसङ्काशं नीलजीमूतसन्निभम्।
प्रादुर्भूतं विषं घोरं संवर्ताग्निसमप्रभम् ॥ 54.56 ॥
1.54.m: “While the ocean was being churned by the great-souled gods and asuras, / looking like serpents and black bees, resembling a dark-blue raincloud, / a terrible poison manifested, equal in splendour to the cosmic fire of destruction,

1.54.s:
kālamṛtyurivodbhūtaṃ yugāntādityavarcasam.
trailokyotsādi sūryābhaṃ prasphurantaṃ samantataḥ .. 54.57 ..
1.54.d:
कालमृत्युरिवोद्भूतं युगान्तादित्यवर्चसम्।
त्रैलोक्योत्सादि सूर्याभं प्रस्फुरन्तं समन्ततः ॥ 54.57 ॥
1.54.m: arisen like Time and Death, with the radiance of the sun at the end of a yuga, / destroying the three worlds, sun-like, flashing all around.

1.54.s:
viṣeṇottiṣṭhamānena kālānalasamatviṣā.
nirdagdho raktagaurāṅgaḥ kṛtakṛṣṇo janārdanaḥ .. 54.58 ..
1.54.d:
विषेणोत्तिष्ठमानेन कालानलसमत्विषा।
निर्दग्धो रक्तगौराङ्गः कृतकृष्णो जनार्दनः ॥ 54.58 ॥
1.54.m: By the rising poison whose lustre was equal to the fire of Time, / Janārdana, whose limbs were fair and ruddy, was scorched and turned black.

1.54.s:
dṛṣṭvā taṃ raktagaurāṅgaṃ kṛtakṛṣṇaṃ janārdanam.
bhītāḥ sarve vayaṃ devāstvāmeva śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ .. 54.59 ..
1.54.d:
दृष्ट्वा तं रक्तगौराङ्गं कृतकृष्णं जनार्दनम्।
भीताः सर्वे वयं देवास्त्वामेव शरणं गताः ॥ 54.59 ॥
1.54.m: Seeing Janārdana, whose limbs were fair and ruddy, turned black, / we gods, all terrified, have fled to you alone for refuge.”

1.54.s:
surāṇāmasurāṇāñca śrutvā vākyaṃ pitāmahaḥ.
pratyuvāca mahātejā lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā .. 54.60 ..
1.54.d:
सुराणामसुराणाञ्च श्रुत्वा वाक्यं पितामहः।
प्रत्युवाच महातेजा लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥ 54.60 ॥
1.54.m: Hearing the speech of the gods and asuras, the Grandfather of great majesty / replied, wishing for the welfare of the worlds:

1.54.s:
śrṛṇudhvaṃ devatāḥ sarve ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ.
yattadagre samutpannaṃ mathyamāne mahodadhau .. 54.61 ..
1.54.d:
श्रृणुध्वं देवताः सर्वे ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः।
यत्तदग्रे समुत्पन्नं मथ्यमाने महोदधौ ॥ 54.61 ॥
1.54.m: “Listen, all you deities and seers whose wealth is asceticism: / that which arose first as the great ocean was churned,

1.54.s:
viṣaṃ kālānalaprakhyaṃ kālakūṭeti viśrutam.
yena prodbhūtamātreṇa kṛtakṛṣṇo janārdanaḥ .. 54.62 ..
1.54.d:
विषं कालानलप्रख्यं कालकूटेति विश्रुतम्।
येन प्रोद्भूतमात्रेण कृतकृष्णो जनार्दनः ॥ 54.62 ॥
1.54.m: the poison resembling the fire of Time, famed as kālakūṭa, / by the mere arising of which Janārdana was turned black—

1.54.s:
tasya viṣṇurahañcāpi sarve te surapuṅgavāḥ.
na śaknuvanti vai soḍhuṃ vegamanye tu śaṅkarāt .. 54.63 ..
1.54.d:
तस्य विष्णुरहञ्चापि सर्वे ते सुरपुङ्गवाः।
न शक्नुवन्ति वै सोढुं वेगमन्ये तु शङ्करात् ॥ 54.63 ॥
1.54.m: Viṣṇu, I, and all these foremost among the gods / cannot bear its force; other than Śaṅkara, [no one can].”

1.54.s:
ityuktvā pajhagarbhābhaḥ pajhayonirayonijaḥ .
tataḥ stotuṃ samārabdho brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ .. 54.64 ..
1.54.d:
इत्युक्त्वा पझगर्भाभः पझयोनिरयोनिजः ।
ततः स्तोतुं समारब्धो ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ॥ 54.64 ॥
1.54.m: Having spoken thus, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / who shines like the lotus-womb, lotus-born and unborn, then began to praise [him]:

1.54.s:
namastubhyaṃ virūpākṣa namaste'nekacakṣuṣe.
namaḥ pinākahastāya vajrahastāya vai namaḥ .. 54.65 ..
1.54.d:
नमस्तुभ्यं विरूपाक्ष नमस्तेऽनेकचक्षुषे।
नमः पिनाकहस्ताय वज्रहस्ताय वै नमः ॥ 54.65 ॥
1.54.m: “Homage to you, odd-eyed one; homage to you who have many eyes; / homage to the one who holds the pināka bow; homage indeed to the thunderbolt-handed one!

1.54.s:
namastrailokyanāthāya bhūtānāmpataye namaḥ.
namaḥ surārisaṃhartre tāpasāya tricakṣuṣe .. 54.66 ..
1.54.d:
नमस्त्रैलोक्यनाथाय भूतानाम्पतये नमः।
नमः सुरारिसंहर्त्रे तापसाय त्रिचक्षुषे ॥ 54.66 ॥
1.54.m: Homage to the lord of the three worlds; homage to the master of beings! / Homage to the destroyer of the foes of the gods, the ascetic with three eyes!

1.54.s:
brahamaṇe caiva rudrāya viṣṇave caiva te namaḥ.
sāṅkhyāya caiva yogāya bhūtagrāmāya vai namaḥ .. 54.67 ..
1.54.d:
ब्रहमणे चैव रुद्राय विष्णवे चैव ते नमः।
साङ्ख्याय चैव योगाय भूतग्रामाय वै नमः ॥ 54.67 ॥
1.54.m: Homage to you as Brahmā, as Rudra, and as Viṣṇu! / Homage to Sāṅkhya, to Yoga, and to the collection of beings!

1.54.s:
manmatāṅgavināśāya kālakālāya vai namaḥ.
rudrāya ca sureśāya devadevāya te namaḥ. 54.68.
kapardine karālāya śaṅkarāya kapāline.
virūpāyaikarūpāya śivāya varadāya ca .. 54.69 ..
1.54.d:
मन्मताङ्गविनाशाय कालकालाय वै नमः।
रुद्राय च सुरेशाय देवदेवाय ते नमः। 54.68.
कपर्दिने करालाय शङ्कराय कपालिने।
विरूपायैकरूपाय शिवाय वरदाय च ॥ 54.69 ॥
1.54.m:
Homage indeed to the destroyer of Manmatha's body, the death of Death!
And homage to you, Rudra, lord of the gods, god of gods!

To the one with matted hair, the terrible one, Śaṅkara, the skull-bearer,
to the multiform, the single-formed, to Śiva, and the bestower of boons.

1.54.s:
tripuraghnāya vandyāya mātṝṇāmpataye namaḥ.
buddhāya caiva śuddhāya muktāya kevalāya ca .. 54.70 ..
1.54.d:
त्रिपुरघ्नाय वन्द्याय मातॄणाम्पतये नमः।
बुद्धाय चैव शुद्धाय मुक्ताय केवलाय च ॥ 54.70 ॥
1.54.m: Homage to the slayer of Tripura, the venerable one, the master of the Mothers, / to the awakened, the pure, the liberated, and the solitary!

1.54.s:
namaḥ kamalahastāya digvāsāya śikhaṇḍine .
loka trayavalidhātre ca candrāya varuṇāya ca .. 54.71 ..
1.54.d:
नमः कमलहस्ताय दिग्वासाय शिखण्डिने ।
लोक त्रयवलिधात्रे च चन्द्राय वरुणाय च ॥ 54.71 ॥
1.54.m: Homage to the lotus-handed one, the sky-clad one, the crested one, / to the provider of offerings for the three worlds, to the Moon, and to Varuṇa!

1.54.s:
agrāya caiva cogrāya viprāyānekacakṣuṣe.
rajase caiva sattvāya tamase'vyaktayonaye .. 54.72 ..
1.54.d:
अग्राय चैव चोग्राय विप्रायानेकचक्षुषे।
रजसे चैव सत्त्वाय तमसेऽव्यक्तयोनये ॥ 54.72 ॥
1.54.m: To the foremost, to the fierce, to the sage, to the multi-eyed, / to rajas, to sattva, to tamas, to the source of the unmanifest!

1.54.s:
nityāyānityarūpāya nityānityāya vai namaḥ.
vyaktāya caivāvyaktāya vyaktāvyaktāya vai namaḥ .. 54.73 ..
1.54.d:
नित्यायानित्यरूपाय नित्यानित्याय वै नमः।
व्यक्ताय चैवाव्यक्ताय व्यक्ताव्यक्ताय वै नमः ॥ 54.73 ॥
1.54.m: Homage to the eternal, to the non-eternal in form, to the eternal-and-non-eternal! / Homage to the manifest, to the unmanifest, to the manifest-and-unmanifest!

1.54.s:
cintyāya caivācintyāya cintyācintyāya vai namaḥ.
bhaktānāmārtināśāya naranārāyaṇāya ca .. 54.74 ..
1.54.d:
चिन्त्याय चैवाचिन्त्याय चिन्त्याचिन्त्याय वै नमः।
भक्तानामार्तिनाशाय नरनारायणाय च ॥ 54.74 ॥
1.54.m: Homage to the conceivable, to the inconceivable, to the conceivable-and-inconceivable, / to the destroyer of the affliction of devotees, and to Nara-Nārāyaṇa!

1.54.s:
umāpriyāya śarvāya nandicakrāṅkitāya ca.
pakṣamāsārddhamāsāya namaḥ saṃvatsarāya ca .. 54.75 ..
1.54.d:
उमाप्रियाय शर्वाय नन्दिचक्राङ्किताय च।
पक्षमासार्द्धमासाय नमः संवत्सराय च ॥ 54.75 ॥
1.54.m: To Umā’s beloved, to Śarva, to the one marked with Nandi’s wheel; / homage to the fortnight, the month, the half-month, and to the year!

1.54.s:
bahurūpāya muṇḍāya daṇḍine'tha varūthine.
namaḥ kapālahastāya digvāsāya śikhaṇiḍane .. 54.76 ..
1.54.d:
बहुरूपाय मुण्डाय दण्डिनेऽथ वरूथिने।
नमः कपालहस्ताय दिग्वासाय शिखणिडने ॥ 54.76 ॥
1.54.m: To the multiform, the shaved-headed, the staff-bearer, and the armoured; / homage to the skull-bearer, the sky-clad, the crested!

1.54.s:
dhvajine rathine caiva yamine brahmacāriṇe.
ṛgyajuḥ sāmavedāya puruṣāyeśvarāya ca.
ityevamādicaritaistubhyaṃ deva namo'stu te .. 54.77 ..
1.54.d:
ध्वजिने रथिने चैव यमिने ब्रह्मचारिणे।
ऋग्यजुः सामवेदाय पुरुषायेश्वराय च।
इत्येवमादिचरितैस्तुभ्यं देव नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 54.77 ॥
1.54.m: To the bannered, the charioteer, the self-controlled, the celibate student; / to the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāmaveda, to the Puruṣa, and to the Lord! / Thus, through these deeds and forms, O God, homage be to you!”

1.54.s: ..śrīmahādeva uvāca..
1.54.d: ॥श्रीमहादेव उवाच॥
1.54.m:
The venerable Mahādeva said:
Thus praised then by the gods, having bowed down, O fair-faced lady—

1.54.s: evaṃ stutastato devaiḥ praṇipatya varānane .. 54.78 ..
1.54.d: एवं स्तुतस्ततो देवैः प्रणिपत्य वरानने ॥ 54.78 ॥

1.54.s:
jñātvā tu bhaktiṃ mama devadevo gaṅgājalāplāvitakeśadeśaḥ.
sūkṣmo'tiyogātiśayādacintyo na hi pluto vyaktamupaiti candraḥ .. 54.79 ..
1.54.d:
ज्ञात्वा तु भक्तिं मम देवदेवो गङ्गाजलाप्लावितकेशदेशः।
सूक्ष्मोऽतियोगातिशयादचिन्त्यो न हि प्लुतो व्यक्तमुपैति चन्द्रः ॥ 54.79 ॥
1.54.m: knowing my devotion, the god of gods, whose hair was flooded by the waters of the Gaṅgā, / subtle through the excellence of intense yoga, inconceivable—for the immersed moon does not appear manifest—

1.54.s:
evaṃ bhagavatā pūrvaṃ brahmaṇā lokakartṛṇā.
stuto'haṃ vividhaiḥ stotrai rvedavedāṅgasambhavaiḥ .. 54.80 ..
1.54.d:
एवं भगवता पूर्वं ब्रह्मणा लोककर्तृणा।
स्तुतोऽहं विविधैः स्तोत्रै र्वेदवेदाङ्गसम्भवैः ॥ 54.80 ॥
1.54.m: in this way, formerly, by the lord Brahmā, the maker of the worlds, / I was praised with various hymns derived from the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

1.54.s:
tataḥ prīto hyahaṃ tasmai brahmaṇe sumahātmane.
tato'haṃ sūkṣmayā vācā pitāmahamathābruvam .. 54.81 ..
1.54.d:
ततः प्रीतो ह्यहं तस्मै ब्रह्मणे सुमहात्मने।
ततोऽहं सूक्ष्मया वाचा पितामहमथाब्रुवम् ॥ 54.81 ॥
1.54.m: Then, pleased with that great-souled Brahmā, / I then addressed the Grandfather in a subtle voice:

1.54.s:
bhagavan bhūtabhavyeśa lokanātha jagatpate.
kiṃ kārye te mayā brahman karttavyaṃ vada suvrata .. 54.82 ..
1.54.d:
भगवन् भूतभव्येश लोकनाथ जगत्पते।
किं कार्ये ते मया ब्रह्मन् कर्त्तव्यं वद सुव्रत ॥ 54.82 ॥
1.54.m: ‘O Lord, ruler of the past and future, lord of the world, master of the universe! / What work of yours must be done by me, O Brahman? Speak, O you of good vows.’

1.54.s:
śrutvā vākyaṃ tato brahmā pratyuvācāmbujekṣaṇaḥ .
bhūtabhavyabhavannātha śrūyatāṃ kāraṇeśvara .. 54.83 ..
1.54.d:
श्रुत्वा वाक्यं ततो ब्रह्मा प्रत्युवाचाम्बुजेक्षणः ।
भूतभव्यभवन्नाथ श्रूयतां कारणेश्वर ॥ 54.83 ॥
1.54.m: Hearing [my] speech, Brahmā, lotus-eyed, then replied: / ‘O ruler of the past, future, and present! O lord of the causes, listen!

1.54.s:
surāsurairmathyamāne payodhāvambujekṣaṇa.
bhagavanmegha saṅkāśaṃ nīlajīmūtasannibham .. 54.84 ..
1.54.d:
सुरासुरैर्मथ्यमाने पयोधावम्बुजेक्षण।
भगवन्मेघ सङ्काशं नीलजीमूतसन्निभम् ॥ 54.84 ॥
1.54.m: As the ocean was being churned by the gods and asuras, O lotus-eyed one, / resembling a cloud, O Lord, looking like a dark-blue raincloud,

1.54.s:
prādurbhūtaṃ viṣaṅghoraṃ saṃvarttāgnisamaprabham.
kālamṛtyurivodbhūtaṃ yugāntādityavarccasam .. 54.85 ..
1.54.d:
प्रादुर्भूतं विषङ्घोरं संवर्त्ताग्निसमप्रभम्।
कालमृत्युरिवोद्भूतं युगान्तादित्यवर्च्चसम् ॥ 54.85 ॥
1.54.m: a terrible poison manifested, equal in splendour to the cosmic fire of destruction, / arisen like Time and Death, with the radiance of the sun at the end of a yuga,

1.54.s:
trailokyotsādi sūryābhaṃ visphurantaṃ samantataḥ.
agre samutthitaṃ tasmin viṣaṅkālānalaprabham .. 54.86 ..
1.54.d:
त्रैलोक्योत्सादि सूर्याभं विस्फुरन्तं समन्ततः।
अग्रे समुत्थितं तस्मिन् विषङ्कालानलप्रभम् ॥ 54.86 ॥
1.54.m: destroying the three worlds, sun-like, flashing all around. / In it arose first the poison possessing the splendour of the fire of Time.

1.54.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā tuṃ vayaṃ sarve bhītāḥ sambhrāntacetasaḥ.
tat pibasva mahādeva lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā .
bhavānagryasya bhoktā vai bhavāṃśvaiva varaḥ prabhuḥ .. 54.87 ..
1.54.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा तुं वयं सर्वे भीताः सम्भ्रान्तचेतसः।
तत् पिबस्व महादेव लोकानां हितकाम्यया ।
भवानग्र्यस्य भोक्ता वै भवांश्वैव वरः प्रभुः ॥ 54.87 ॥
1.54.m: Seeing it, all of us became frightened, our minds bewildered. / Therefore drink it, Mahādeva, out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds! / You indeed are the enjoyer of the foremost portion, and you are the supreme lord.

1.54.s:
tvāmṛte'nyo mahādeva viṣaṃ soḍhuṃ na vidyate .
nāsti kaścit pumān śaktastrailokyeṣu ca gīyate .. 54.88 ..
1.54.d:
त्वामृतेऽन्यो महादेव विषं सोढुं न विद्यते ।
नास्ति कश्चित् पुमान् शक्तस्त्रैलोक्येषु च गीयते ॥ 54.88 ॥
1.54.m: Apart from you, O Mahādeva, none is found to bear the poison; / no man in the three worlds is sung of as capable [of this].’

1.54.s:
evaṃ tasya vacaḥ śrutvā brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ.
bāḍhamityeva tadvākyaṃ pratigṛhya varānane .. 54.89 ..
1.54.d:
एवं तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मणः परमेष्ठिनः।
बाढमित्येव तद्वाक्यं प्रतिगृह्य वरानने ॥ 54.89 ॥
1.54.m: Having heard this word of Brahmā Parameṣṭhin, / accepting that speech, saying “So be it,” O fair-faced one,

1.54.s:
tato'haṃ pātumārabdho viṣamantakasannibham.
pibato me mahāghoraṃ viṣaṃ surabhayaṅkaram.
kaṇṭhaḥ samabhavattūrṇaṃ kṛṣṇo me varavarṇini .. 54.90 ..
1.54.d:
ततोऽहं पातुमारब्धो विषमन्तकसन्निभम्।
पिबतो मे महाघोरं विषं सुरभयङ्करम्।
कण्ठः समभवत्तूर्णं कृष्णो मे वरवर्णिनि ॥ 54.90 ॥
1.54.m: I then began to drink the poison resembling Death. / As I drank the exceedingly terrible poison that terrified the gods, / my throat quickly turned black, O woman of excellent complexion.”

1.54.s:
taṃdṛṣṭvo tpalapatrābhaṃ kaṇṭhe saktamivoragam .
takṣakaṃ nāgarājānaṃ lelihānamiva sthitam .. 54.91 ..
1.54.d:
तंदृष्ट्वो त्पलपत्राभं कण्ठे सक्तमिवोरगम् ।
तक्षकं नागराजानं लेलिहानमिव स्थितम् ॥ 54.91 ॥
1.54.m: Seeing that [spot], resembling a blue lotus petal, clinging like a snake upon my throat, / resting like Takṣaka, king of snakes, darting his tongue,

1.54.s:
athovāca mahātejā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ.
śobhase tvaṃ mahādeva kaṇṭhenānena suvrata .. 54.92 ..
1.54.d:
अथोवाच महातेजा ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः।
शोभसे त्वं महादेव कण्ठेनानेन सुव्रत ॥ 54.92 ॥
1.54.m: then Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, possessing great splendour, said: / 'O Mahādeva, of noble vows, you are adorned by this throat!'

1.54.s:
tatastasya vacaḥ śrutvā mayā girivarātmaje.
paśyatāṃ devasaṅgānāṃ daityānāñca varānane .. 54.93 ..
1.54.d:
ततस्तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा मया गिरिवरात्मजे।
पश्यतां देवसङ्गानां दैत्यानाञ्च वरानने ॥ 54.93 ॥
1.54.m: Then, having heard his words, O daughter of the best of mountains, / while the hosts of gods and daityas looked on, O fair-faced lady,

1.54.s:
yakṣagandharvabhūtānāṃ piśācoragarakṣasām.
dhṛtaṃ kaṇṭhe viṣaṃ ghoraṃ nīlakaṇṭastato hyaham .. 54.94 ..
1.54.d:
यक्षगन्धर्वभूतानां पिशाचोरगरक्षसाम्।
धृतं कण्ठे विषं घोरं नीलकण्टस्ततो ह्यहम् ॥ 54.94 ॥
1.54.m: [and] the yakṣas, gandharvas, bhūtas, piśācas, uragas, and rākṣasas, / the terrible poison was held in my throat; therefore, indeed, I am Nīlakaṇṭha.

1.54.s:
tat kālakūṭaṃ viṣamugratejaḥ kaṇṭhe mayā parvatarājaputri.
niveśyamānaṃ suradaityasaṅgho dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayamājagāma .. 54.95 ..
1.54.d:
तत् कालकूटं विषमुग्रतेजः कण्ठे मया पर्वतराजपुत्रि।
निवेश्यमानं सुरदैत्यसङ्घो दृष्ट्वा परं विस्मयमाजगाम ॥ 54.95 ॥
1.54.m: O daughter of the king of mountains, seeing that Kālakūṭa poison of fierce splendour / being placed into my throat, the host of gods and daityas was struck with the greatest wonder.

1.54.s:
tataḥ suragaṇāḥ sarve sadaityoragarākṣasāḥ.
ūcuḥ prāñcalayo bhūtvā mattamātaṅgagāmini .. 54.96 ..
1.54.d:
ततः सुरगणाः सर्वे सदैत्योरगराक्षसाः।
ऊचुः प्राञ्चलयो भूत्वा मत्तमातङ्गगामिनि ॥ 54.96 ॥
1.54.m: Then all the hosts of gods, together with the daityas, uragas, and rākṣasas, / having joined their palms, spoke, O lady with the gait of an elephant in rut:

1.54.s:
aho balaṃ vīryaparākramaste aho punaryogabalaṃ tavaiva.
aho prabhutvaṃ tava devadeva gaṅgājalāsphālitamuktakeśa .. 54.97 ..
1.54.d:
अहो बलं वीर्यपराक्रमस्ते अहो पुनर्योगबलं तवैव।
अहो प्रभुत्वं तव देवदेव गङ्गाजलास्फालितमुक्तकेश ॥ 54.97 ॥
1.54.m: 'Ah, what strength, valour, and prowess are yours! Ah, the power of your yoga indeed! / Ah, what sovereignty is yours, O god of gods, whose unloosened hair is struck by the waters of the Gaṅgā!

1.54.s:
tvameva viṣṇuścaturānanastvaṃ tvameva mṛtyu rvaradastvameva.
tvameva sūryo rajanīkaraśca tvameva bhūmiḥ salilaṃ tvameva .. 54.98 ..
1.54.d:
त्वमेव विष्णुश्चतुराननस्त्वं त्वमेव मृत्यु र्वरदस्त्वमेव।
त्वमेव सूर्यो रजनीकरश्च त्वमेव भूमिः सलिलं त्वमेव ॥ 54.98 ॥
1.54.m: You alone are Viṣṇu, you are the four-faced [Brahmā], you alone are death, you alone are the granter of boons; / you alone are the sun and the maker of the night; you alone are the earth, you alone are water;

1.54.s:
tvameva yajño niyamastvameva tvameva bhūtaṃ bhavitā tvameva.
tvameva cādi rnidhanaṃ tvameva sthūlaśca sūkṣmaḥ puruṣastvameva .. 54.99 ..
1.54.d:
त्वमेव यज्ञो नियमस्त्वमेव त्वमेव भूतं भविता त्वमेव।
त्वमेव चादि र्निधनं त्वमेव स्थूलश्च सूक्ष्मः पुरुषस्त्वमेव ॥ 54.99 ॥
1.54.m: you alone are the sacrifice, you alone are observance; you alone are what has been, you alone are what shall be; / you alone are the beginning, you alone are destruction; you alone are the gross, the subtle, and the Puruṣa;

1.54.s:
tvameva sūkṣmasya parasya sūkṣmastvameva vahniḥ pavanastvameva.
tvameva sarvasya carācarasya lokasya karttā pralaye ca goptā .. 54.100 ..
1.54.d:
त्वमेव सूक्ष्मस्य परस्य सूक्ष्मस्त्वमेव वह्निः पवनस्त्वमेव।
त्वमेव सर्वस्य चराचरस्य लोकस्य कर्त्ता प्रलये च गोप्ता ॥ 54.100 ॥
1.54.m: you alone are subtler than the subtle transcendent; you alone are fire, you alone are the wind; / you are the maker of all the moving and unmoving world, and its protector at the time of dissolution.'

1.54.s:
itīdamuktvā vacanaṃ surendrāḥ pragṛhya somaṃ praṇipatya mūrdnā.
gatā vimānairanigṛhya vegairmahātmano merumupetya sarve .. 54.101 ..
1.54.d:
इतीदमुक्त्वा वचनं सुरेन्द्राः प्रगृह्य सोमं प्रणिपत्य मूर्द्ना।
गता विमानैरनिगृह्य वेगैर्महात्मनो मेरुमुपेत्य सर्वे ॥ 54.101 ॥
1.54.m: Having spoken these words, the lords of the gods took the soma, bowed down their heads, / and all those noble beings departed on celestial chariots of uncurbed speed, having approached Mount Meru.

1.54.s:
ityetatparamaṃ guhyaṃ puṇyātpuṇyamahattaram.
nīlakaṇṭheti yat proktaṃ vikhyātaṃ lokaviśrutam .. 54.102 ..
1.54.d:
इत्येतत्परमं गुह्यं पुण्यात्पुण्यमहत्तरम्।
नीलकण्ठेति यत् प्रोक्तं विख्यातं लोकविश्रुतम् ॥ 54.102 ॥
1.54.m: This is the supreme secret, holier than holy, / which is called 'Nīlakaṇṭha', celebrated and famous across the worlds.

1.54.s:
svayaṃ svayambhuvā proktāṃ puṇyāṃ pāpapraṇāśanīm.
yastu dhārayate nityamenāṃ brahmodbhavāṃ kathām.
tasyāhaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi phalaṃ vai vipulaṃ mahat .. 54.103 ..
1.54.d:
स्वयं स्वयम्भुवा प्रोक्तां पुण्यां पापप्रणाशनीम्।
यस्तु धारयते नित्यमेनां ब्रह्मोद्भवां कथाम्।
तस्याहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि फलं वै विपुलं महत् ॥ 54.103 ॥
1.54.m: Whoever constantly bears in mind this holy narrative that destroys sin, / spoken by Svayambhū himself and originating from Brahmā, / to him I shall declare the immense and great fruit:

1.54.s:
viṣaṃ tasya varārohe sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamantathā.
gātraṃ prāpya ca suśroṇi kṣipraṃ tat pratihanyate .. 54.104 ..
1.54.d:
विषं तस्य वरारोहे स्थावरं जङ्गमन्तथा।
गात्रं प्राप्य च सुश्रोणि क्षिप्रं तत् प्रतिहन्यते ॥ 54.104 ॥
1.54.m: His poison, both inanimate and animate, O fair-hipped lady, / upon reaching his body, is quickly nullified, O fair-hipped one.

1.54.s:
śamayatyaśubhaṃ ghoraṃ duḥsvapnañcāpakarṣati.
strīṣu vallabhatāṃ yāti sabhāyāṃ pārthivasya ca .. 54.105 ..
1.54.d:
शमयत्यशुभं घोरं दुःस्वप्नञ्चापकर्षति।
स्त्रीषु वल्लभतां याति सभायां पार्थिवस्य च ॥ 54.105 ॥
1.54.m: It pacifies terrible misfortune and wards off bad dreams; / he becomes beloved among women and in the assembly of the king;

1.54.s:
vivāde jayamāpnoti yuddhe śūratvameva ca.
gacchataḥ kṣemamadhvānaṃ gṛhe ca nityasampadaḥ .. 54.106 ..
1.54.d:
विवादे जयमाप्नोति युद्धे शूरत्वमेव च।
गच्छतः क्षेममध्वानं गृहे च नित्यसम्पदः ॥ 54.106 ॥
1.54.m: he gains victory in dispute, and courage in battle; / his journey proceeds in safety, and prosperity dwells constantly in his home.

1.54.s:
śarīrabhede vakṣyāmi gatiṃ tasya varānane.
nīlakaṇṭho haricchamaśruḥ śaśāṅkāṅkitamūrddhajaḥ .. 54.107 ..
1.54.d:
शरीरभेदे वक्ष्यामि गतिं तस्य वरानने।
नीलकण्ठो हरिच्छमश्रुः शशाङ्काङ्कितमूर्द्धजः ॥ 54.107 ॥
1.54.m: At the dissolution of the body, I will declare his destiny, O fair-faced lady: / having a blue throat, a tawny beard, and hair adorned with the moon,

1.54.s:
tryakṣastriśūlapāṇiśca vṛṣayānaḥ pinākadhṛk.
nandhitulyabalaḥ śrīmān nanditulyaparākramaḥ .. 54.108 ..
1.54.d:
त्र्यक्षस्त्रिशूलपाणिश्च वृषयानः पिनाकधृक्।
नन्धितुल्यबलः श्रीमान् नन्दितुल्यपराक्रमः ॥ 54.108 ॥
1.54.m: three-eyed, holding a trident in hand, riding a bull, wielding the Pināka, / equal in strength to Nandin, glorious, equal in prowess to Nandi,

1.54.s:
vicaratyacirāt sarvān sarvalokānmamājñayā .
na hanyate gatistasya anilasya yathāmbare.
mama tulyabalo bhūtvā tiṣṭhatyābhūtasamplavam .. 54.109 ..
1.54.d:
विचरत्यचिरात् सर्वान् सर्वलोकान्ममाज्ञया ।
न हन्यते गतिस्तस्य अनिलस्य यथाम्बरे।
मम तुल्यबलो भूत्वा तिष्ठत्याभूतसम्प्लवम् ॥ 54.109 ॥
1.54.m: he swiftly wanders across all worlds at my command; / his path is never obstructed, just as that of the wind in the sky; / having become equal in strength to me, he abides until the deluge of beings.

1.54.s:
mama bhaktā varārohe ye ca śrṛṇvanti mānavāḥ.
teṣāṃ gatiṃ pravakṣyāmi iha loke paratra ca .. 54.110 ..
1.54.d:
मम भक्ता वरारोहे ये च श्रृण्वन्ति मानवाः।
तेषां गतिं प्रवक्ष्यामि इह लोके परत्र च ॥ 54.110 ॥
1.54.m: To those humans who are my devotees, O fair-hipped lady, and who listen, / I will declare their destiny in this world and the hereafter:

1.54.s:
brāhmaṇo vedamāpnoti kṣatriyo jayate mahīm.
vaiśyastu labhate lābhaṃ śūdraḥ sukhamavāpnuyāt .. 54.111 ..
1.54.d:
ब्राह्मणो वेदमाप्नोति क्षत्रियो जयते महीम्।
वैश्यस्तु लभते लाभं शूद्रः सुखमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 54.111 ॥
1.54.m: A brāhmaṇa attains the Veda, a kṣatriya conquers the earth, / a vaiśya obtains profit, and a śūdra attains happiness.

1.54.s:
vyādhito mucyate rogādbaddho mucyeta bandhanāt.
gurviṇī labhate putraṃ kanyā vindati satpatim.
naṣṭañca labhate sarvamihaloke paratra ca .. 54.112 ..
1.54.d:
व्याधितो मुच्यते रोगाद्बद्धो मुच्येत बन्धनात्।
गुर्विणी लभते पुत्रं कन्या विन्दति सत्पतिम्।
नष्टञ्च लभते सर्वमिहलोके परत्र च ॥ 54.112 ॥
1.54.m: The diseased is freed from sickness, the bound is freed from bondage; / a pregnant woman obtains a son, a maiden finds a good husband; / and whatever was lost is recovered in this world and the hereafter.

1.54.s:
gavāṃ śatasahasrasya samyagdattasya yat phalam.
tat phalaṃ bhavati śrutvā vibhordivyāmimāṃ kathām .. 54.113 ..
1.54.d:
गवां शतसहस्रस्य सम्यग्दत्तस्य यत् फलम्।
तत् फलं भवति श्रुत्वा विभोर्दिव्यामिमां कथाम् ॥ 54.113 ॥
1.54.m: Whatever fruit is attained from a hundred thousand cows properly given, / that same fruit comes from hearing this divine narrative of the lord.

1.54.s:
pādaṃ vā yadi vāpyarddhaṃ ślokaṃ ślokārddhameva vā.
yastu dhārayate nityaṃ rudralokaṃ sa gacchati .. 54.114 ..
1.54.d:
पादं वा यदि वाप्यर्द्धं श्लोकं श्लोकार्द्धमेव वा।
यस्तु धारयते नित्यं रुद्रलोकं स गच्छति ॥ 54.114 ॥
1.54.m: Whether a quarter, a half, a verse, or even half a verse, / whoever constantly holds it in mind goes to the world of Rudra.

1.54.s:
kathāmimāṃ puṇyaphalādiyuktāṃ nivedya devyāḥ śaśibaddha mūrddhajaḥ.
vṛṣasya pṛṣṭhena sahomayā prabhurjagāma kiṣkindhaguhāṃ guhapriyaḥ .. 54.115 ..
1.54.d:
कथामिमां पुण्यफलादियुक्तां निवेद्य देव्याः शशिबद्ध मूर्द्धजः।
वृषस्य पृष्ठेन सहोमया प्रभुर्जगाम किष्किन्धगुहां गुहप्रियः ॥ 54.115 ॥
1.54.m: Having recounted to the goddess this narrative endowed with holy rewards, the lord whose hair binds the moon, who delights in Guha, / went upon the back of his bull together with Umā to the cave of Kiṣkindha.

1.54.s:
krāntaṃ mayā pāpaharaṃ mahāpadaṃ nivedya tebhyaḥ pradadau prabhañjanaḥ.
adhītya sarvaṃ tvakhilaṃ sulakṣaṇaṃ jagāma ādityapathaṃ dvijottamaḥ .. 54.116 ..
1.54.d:
क्रान्तं मया पापहरं महापदं निवेद्य तेभ्यः प्रददौ प्रभञ्जनः।
अधीत्य सर्वं त्वखिलं सुलक्षणं जगाम आदित्यपथं द्विजोत्तमः ॥ 54.116 ॥
1.54.m: Prabhañcana, having proclaimed the great realm that destroys sins and is traversed by me, imparted it to them; / having studied the whole of it completely with its auspicious marks, that best of the twice-born went along the path of the sun.

1.54.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyu prokte nīlakaṇṭhastavo nāma catuḥ pañcāśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 54 ..
1.54.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायु प्रोक्ते नीलकण्ठस्तवो नाम चतुः पञ्चाशोऽध्यायः ॥ 54 ॥
1.54.m: Thus ends the fifty-fourth chapter, called 'Praise of Nīlakaṇṭha', in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa uttered by Vāyu.

1.55.s: ..ṛṣaya ūcuḥ..
1.55.d: ॥ऋषय ऊचुः॥
1.55.m:
The seers said:
Who is superior in virtues, actions, and powers, O best of speakers?
We wish to hear in full the wondrous expansion of [his] qualities.

1.55.s:
guṇakarmaprabhāvaiśca ko'dhiko vadatāṃ varaḥ.
śrotumicchāmahe samyagāścaryaṃ guṇavistaram .. 55.1 ..
1.55.d:
गुणकर्मप्रभावैश्च कोऽधिको वदतां वरः।
श्रोतुमिच्छामहे सम्यगाश्चर्यं गुणविस्तरम् ॥ 55.1 ॥

1.55.s: ..sūta uvāca..
1.55.d: ॥सूत उवाच॥
1.55.m:
The Sūta said:
In this regard also they cite this ancient legend:
the greatness of Mahādeva and the omnipresent majesty of that great soul.

1.55.s:
atrāpyudāharantīmamiti hāsaṃ purātanam .
mahādevasya māhātmyaṃ vibhutvañca mahātmanaḥ .. 55.2 ..
1.55.d:
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममिति हासं पुरातनम् ।
महादेवस्य माहात्म्यं विभुत्वञ्च महात्मनः ॥ 55.2 ॥

1.55.s:
pūrvaṃ trailokyavijaye viṣṇunā samudāhṛtam.
baliṃ baddhvā mahaujāstu trailokyādhi patiḥ purā .. 55.3 ..
1.55.d:
पूर्वं त्रैलोक्यविजये विष्णुना समुदाहृतम्।
बलिं बद्ध्वा महौजास्तु त्रैलोक्याधि पतिः पुरा ॥ 55.3 ॥
1.55.m: formerly recounted by Viṣṇu at the conquest of the three worlds, / when, of old, having bound Bali, the lord of the three worlds possessed great splendour.

1.55.s:
praṇaṣṭeṣu ca daityeṣu prahṛṣṭe ca śacīpatau.
athājagmuḥ prabhuṃ draṣṭuṃ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ .. 55.4 ..
1.55.d:
प्रणष्टेषु च दैत्येषु प्रहृष्टे च शचीपतौ।
अथाजग्मुः प्रभुं द्रष्टुं सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः ॥ 55.4 ॥
1.55.m: When the daityas were destroyed and the husband of Śacī rejoiced, / then all the gods together with Indra came to see the Lord,

1.55.s:
yatrāste viśvarūpātmā kṣīrodasya samī pataḥ.
siddhabrahmarṣayo yakṣā gandharvāpsarasāṅgaṇāḥ .. 55.5 ..
1.55.d:
यत्रास्ते विश्वरूपात्मा क्षीरोदस्य समी पतः।
सिद्धब्रह्मर्षयो यक्षा गन्धर्वाप्सरसाङ्गणाः ॥ 55.5 ॥
1.55.m: where the embodiment of universal form resides near the milk-ocean: / the siddhas, brahmarṣis, yakṣas, and the hosts of gandharvas and apsarases,

1.55.s:
nāgā devarṣayaścaiva nadyaḥ sarve ca parvatāḥ.
abhigamya mahātmānaṃ stuvanti puruṣaṃ harim .. 55.6 ..
1.55.d:
नागा देवर्षयश्चैव नद्यः सर्वे च पर्वताः।
अभिगम्य महात्मानं स्तुवन्ति पुरुषं हरिम् ॥ 55.6 ॥
1.55.m: the nāgas, devarṣis, all the rivers, and the mountains, / having approached the noble Puruṣa Hari, praise him:

1.55.s:
tvaṃ dhātā tvañca karttā'sya tvaṃ lokān sṛjasi prabho.
tvatprasādācca kalyāṇaṃ prāptaṃ trailokyamavyayam.
asurāśca jitāḥ sarve balirbaddhaśca vai tvayā .. 55.7 ..
1.55.d:
त्वं धाता त्वञ्च कर्त्ताऽस्य त्वं लोकान् सृजसि प्रभो।
त्वत्प्रसादाच्च कल्याणं प्राप्तं त्रैलोक्यमव्ययम्।
असुराश्च जिताः सर्वे बलिर्बद्धश्च वै त्वया ॥ 55.7 ॥
1.55.m: 'You are the supporter and the maker of this [universe]; you create the worlds, O Lord. / By your grace the auspicious and imperishable three worlds have been attained; / all the asuras have been conquered, and Bali has indeed been bound by you.'

1.55.s:
eva muktaḥ surairviṣṇuḥ siddhaiśca paramarṣibhiḥ.
pratyuvāca tato devān sarvāṃstān puruṣottamaḥ .. 55.8 ..
1.55.d:
एव मुक्तः सुरैर्विष्णुः सिद्धैश्च परमर्षिभिः।
प्रत्युवाच ततो देवान् सर्वांस्तान् पुरुषोत्तमः ॥ 55.8 ॥
1.55.m: Thus addressed by the gods, the siddhas, and the supreme seers, / Viṣṇu, the supreme Puruṣa, then answered all those gods:

1.55.s:
śrūyatāmabhidhāsyāmi kāraṇaṃ surasattamāḥ.
yaḥ sraṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ kālaḥ kālakaraḥ prabhuḥ .. 55.9 ..
1.55.d:
श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि कारणं सुरसत्तमाः।
यः स्रष्टा सर्वभूतानां कालः कालकरः प्रभुः ॥ 55.9 ॥
1.55.m: 'Listen, O best of gods, I will declare the ultimate cause; / he who is the creator of all beings, Time, the maker of time, the Lord,

1.55.s:
yena hi brahmaṇā sārddhaṃ sṛṣṭā lokāśca māyayā.
tasyaiva ca prasādena ādau siddhatvamāgatam .. 55.10 ..
1.55.d:
येन हि ब्रह्मणा सार्द्धं सृष्टा लोकाश्च मायया।
तस्यैव च प्रसादेन आदौ सिद्धत्वमागतम् ॥ 55.10 ॥
1.55.m: by whom together with Brahmā the worlds were created through māyā; / and by his grace alone was perfection attained in the beginning.

1.55.s:
purā tamasi cāvyakte trailokye grāsite mayā.
udarastheṣu bhūteṣu loke'haṃ śayitastadā .. 55.11 ..
1.55.d:
पुरा तमसि चाव्यक्ते त्रैलोक्ये ग्रासिते मया।
उदरस्थेषु भूतेषु लोकेऽहं शयितस्तदा ॥ 55.11 ॥
1.55.m: Formerly, when the three worlds had been swallowed by darkness and the unmanifest, and consumed by me, / and beings were situated in my belly, I was then sleeping in the world;

1.55.s:
sahasraśīrṣā bhūtvā ca sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt.
śaṅkhacakragadā pāṇiḥ śayito vimale'mbhasi .. 55.12 ..
1.55.d:
सहस्रशीर्षा भूत्वा च सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात्।
शङ्खचक्रगदा पाणिः शयितो विमलेऽम्भसि ॥ 55.12 ॥
1.55.m: having become thousand-headed, thousand-eyed, and thousand-footed, / holding the conch, discus, and mace in hand, I lay asleep on the spotless water.'"

1.55.s:
etasminnantare dūrāt paśyāmi hyamitaprabham.
śatasūryapratīkāśaṃ jvalantaṃ svena tejasā .. 55.13 ..
1.55.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे दूरात् पश्यामि ह्यमितप्रभम्।
शतसूर्यप्रतीकाशं ज्वलन्तं स्वेन तेजसा ॥ 55.13 ॥
1.55.m: In the meantime, from afar, I saw one of boundless radiance, / resembling a hundred suns, blazing with his own splendour,

1.55.s:
caturvakraṃ mahā yogaṃ puruṣaṃ kāñcanaprabham.
kṛṣṇājinadharaṃ devaṃ kamaṇḍaluvibhūṣitam.
nimeṣāntaramātreṇa prāpto'sau puruṣottamaḥ .. 55.14 ..
1.55.d:
चतुर्वक्रं महा योगं पुरुषं काञ्चनप्रभम्।
कृष्णाजिनधरं देवं कमण्डलुविभूषितम्।
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण प्राप्तोऽसौ पुरुषोत्तमः ॥ 55.14 ॥
1.55.m: four-faced, of great yoga, a person glowing like gold, / a god wearing a black antelope skin and adorned with a water-pot. / In the mere twinkling of an eye, that supreme person arrived.

1.55.s:
tato māmabravīdbrahmā sarvaloka namaskṛtaḥ.
kastvaṃ kuto vā kiñceha tiṣṭhase vada me vibho .. 55.15 ..
1.55.d:
ततो मामब्रवीद्ब्रह्मा सर्वलोक नमस्कृतः।
कस्त्वं कुतो वा किञ्चेह तिष्ठसे वद मे विभो ॥ 55.15 ॥
1.55.m: Then Brahmā, who is bowed to by all worlds, said to me: / 'Who are you, or whence [do you come], and why do you remain here? Tell me, O Lord!'

1.55.s:
ahaṃ karttā'smi lokānāṃ svayambūrviśvatomukhaḥ.
evamuktastadā dena brahmaṇāhamuvāca tam .. 55.16 ..
1.55.d:
अहं कर्त्ताऽस्मि लोकानां स्वयम्बूर्विश्वतोमुखः।
एवमुक्तस्तदा देन ब्रह्मणाहमुवाच तम् ॥ 55.16 ॥
1.55.m: 'I am the creator of the worlds, the self-existent, facing every direction.' / Having been addressed thus by the god Brahmā, I said to him:

1.55.s:
ahaṃ karttā ca lokānāṃ saṃharttā ca punaḥ punaḥ.
evaṃ sambhāṣamāṇābhyāṃ parasparajayaiṣiṇām.
uttarāṃ diśamāsthāya jvālā dṛṣṭāpyadhiṣṭhitā .. 55.17 ..
1.55.d:
अहं कर्त्ता च लोकानां संहर्त्ता च पुनः पुनः।
एवं सम्भाषमाणाभ्यां परस्परजयैषिणाम्।
उत्तरां दिशमास्थाय ज्वाला दृष्टाप्यधिष्ठिता ॥ 55.17 ॥
1.55.m: 'I too am the creator of the worlds, and their destroyer again and again.' / As the two [of us], desiring victory over each other, were thus conversing, / a flame was seen stationed in the northern quarter.

1.55.s:
jvālāntatastāmālokya vismittau ca tadānayoḥ .
tejasā caiva tenātha sarvaṃ jyotiḥkṛtaṃ jalam .. 55.18 ..
1.55.d:
ज्वालान्ततस्तामालोक्य विस्मित्तौ च तदानयोः ।
तेजसा चैव तेनाथ सर्वं ज्योतिःकृतं जलम् ॥ 55.18 ॥
1.55.m: Beholding that flame extending to the horizon, the two of them were astonished; / and by that brilliance, all the water was turned into light.

1.55.s:
varddhamāne tadā vahnāvatyantaparamādbhute.
atidudrāva tāṃ jvālāṃ brahmā cāhañca satvaraḥ .. 55.19 ..
1.55.d:
वर्द्धमाने तदा वह्नावत्यन्तपरमाद्भुते।
अतिदुद्राव तां ज्वालां ब्रह्मा चाहञ्च सत्वरः ॥ 55.19 ॥
1.55.m: As that fire, exceedingly and supremely wondrous, was growing, / Brahmā and I both rushed swiftly toward that flame.

1.55.s:
divaṃ bhūmiñca viṣṭabhya tiṣṭhantaṃ jvālamaṇḍalam.
tasya jvālasya madhye tu paśyāvo vipulaprabham .. 55.20 ..
1.55.d:
दिवं भूमिञ्च विष्टभ्य तिष्ठन्तं ज्वालमण्डलम्।
तस्य ज्वालस्य मध्ये तु पश्यावो विपुलप्रभम् ॥ 55.20 ॥
1.55.m: To the orb of flame that stood spanning heaven and earth, / in the midst of that flame we both beheld [something] of vast brilliance:

1.55.s:
prādeśamātramavyaktaṃ liṅgaṃ paramadīpitam.
na ca tatkāñcanaṃ madhye na śailaṃ na ca rājatam .. 55.21 ..
1.55.d:
प्रादेशमात्रमव्यक्तं लिङ्गं परमदीपितम्।
न च तत्काञ्चनं मध्ये न शैलं न च राजतम् ॥ 55.21 ॥
1.55.m: a unmanifest liṅga, a span in size, supremely blazing; / and it was not made of gold in the center, nor of stone, nor of silver,

1.55.s:
anirddeśyamacintyañca lakṣyālakṣyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ.
mahaujasaṃ mahāghoraṃ varddhamānaṃ bhṛśaṃ tadā.
jvālāmālāyataṃ nyastaṃ sarvabhūtabhayaṅkaram .. 55.22 ..
1.55.d:
अनिर्द्देश्यमचिन्त्यञ्च लक्ष्यालक्ष्यं पुनः पुनः।
महौजसं महाघोरं वर्द्धमानं भृशं तदा।
ज्वालामालायतं न्यस्तं सर्वभूतभयङ्करम् ॥ 55.22 ॥
1.55.m: indescribable and unthinkable, repeatedly visible and invisible, / of great majesty, exceedingly terrifying, growing vehemently at that time, / surrounded by garlands of flame, causing terror to all beings.

1.55.s:
asya liṅgasya yo'ntaṃ vai gacchate mantrakāraṇam.
ghora rūpiṇamatyarthaṃ bhindantamiva rodasī .. 55.23 ..
1.55.d:
अस्य लिङ्गस्य योऽन्तं वै गच्छते मन्त्रकारणम्।
घोर रूपिणमत्यर्थं भिन्दन्तमिव रोदसी ॥ 55.23 ॥
1.55.m: [Saying,] 'Whoever reaches the end of this liṅga, the cause of mantras, / terrifying in form, seemingly tearing apart heaven and earth,'

1.55.s:
tato māmabravīdbrahmā adho gaccha tvatandritaḥ.
antamasya vijānīmo liṅgasya tu mahātmanaḥ .. 55.24 ..
1.55.d:
ततो मामब्रवीद्ब्रह्मा अधो गच्छ त्वतन्द्रितः।
अन्तमस्य विजानीमो लिङ्गस्य तु महात्मनः ॥ 55.24 ॥
1.55.m: then Brahmā said to me: 'Go downward without slacking! / Let us discover the end of this great-souled liṅga.

1.55.s:
ahamūrddhvaṃ gamiṣyāmi yāvadanto'sya dṛśyate.
tadā tau samayaṃ kṛtvā gatāvūrddhvamadhaśca ha .. 55.25 ..
1.55.d:
अहमूर्द्ध्वं गमिष्यामि यावदन्तोऽस्य दृश्यते।
तदा तौ समयं कृत्वा गतावूर्द्ध्वमधश्च ह ॥ 55.25 ॥
1.55.m: I shall go upward until its end is seen.' / Then, having made an agreement, the two went upward and downward.

1.55.s:
tato varṣasahasrantu ahaṃ punaradho gataḥ.
na ca paśyāmi tasyāntaṃ bhītaścāhaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 55.26 ..
1.55.d:
ततो वर्षसहस्रन्तु अहं पुनरधो गतः।
न च पश्यामि तस्यान्तं भीतश्चाहं न संशयः ॥ 55.26 ॥
1.55.m: Then for a thousand years I went downward, / yet I did not see its end, and I was afraid, without a doubt.

1.55.s:
tathā brahmā ca śrāntaśca na cāntantasya paśyati.
samāgato mayā sārddhaṃ tatraiva ca mahāmbhasi .. 55.27 ..
1.55.d:
तथा ब्रह्मा च श्रान्तश्च न चान्तन्तस्य पश्यति।
समागतो मया सार्द्धं तत्रैव च महाम्भसि ॥ 55.27 ॥
1.55.m: Likewise Brahmā, weary, did not see its end; / he met with me right there in the great water.

1.55.s: tato vismayamāpannāvubhau tasya mahātmanaḥ ..
1.55.d: ततो विस्मयमापन्नावुभौ तस्य महात्मनः ॥
1.55.m:
Then both of them, struck with wonder, deluded by the māyā
of that great soul, remained bereft of consciousness.

1.55.s: māyayā mohitau tena naṣṭasaṃjñau vyavasthitau .. 55.28 ..
1.55.d: मायया मोहितौ तेन नष्टसंज्ञौ व्यवस्थितौ ॥ 55.28 ॥

1.55.s:
tato dhyānagatantatra īśvaraṃ sarvatomukham.
prabhavaṃ nidhaṉañcaiva lokānāṃ prabhumavyayam .. 55.29 ..
1.55.d:
ततो ध्यानगतन्तत्र ईश्वरं सर्वतोमुखम्।
प्रभवं निधṉअञ्चैव लोकानां प्रभुमव्ययम् ॥ 55.29 ॥
1.55.m: Then, [beholding] in meditation the Lord present there, facing every direction, / the origin and destruction of the worlds, the imperishable master,

1.55.s:
brahmāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā tasmai śarvāya śūline.
mahābhairavanādāya bhīmarūpāya daṃṣṭriṇe.
avyaktāya mahāntāya namaskāraṃ prakurmahe .. 55.30 ..
1.55.d:
ब्रह्माञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा तस्मै शर्वाय शूलिने।
महाभैरवनादाय भीमरूपाय दंष्ट्रिणे।
अव्यक्ताय महान्ताय नमस्कारं प्रकुर्महे ॥ 55.30 ॥
1.55.m: Brahmā and I, with hands folded in reverence, pay homage to him, to Śarva, the bearer of the trident, / who makes a great, terrifying sound, who has a dreadful form, fanged, / unmanifest, and supreme:

1.55.s:
namo'stu te lokasureśa deva namo'stu te bhūtapate mahāṃśca.
namo'stu te śāśvata siddhayone namo'stu te sarvajagatpratiṣṭha .. 55.31 ..
1.55.d:
नमोऽस्तु ते लोकसुरेश देव नमोऽस्तु ते भूतपते महांश्च।
नमोऽस्तु ते शाश्वत सिद्धयोने नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वजगत्प्रतिष्ठ ॥ 55.31 ॥
1.55.m: 'Homage be to you, Lord of the worlds and the gods, O god! Homage be to you, Lord of beings, O great one! / Homage be to you, eternal source of the siddhas! Homage be to you, foundation of the entire universe!

1.55.s:
parameṣṭhī paraṃ brahma akṣaraṃ paramaṃ padam.
śreṣṭhastvaṃ vāmadevaśca rudraḥ skandaḥ śivaḥ prabhuḥ .. 55.32 ..
1.55.d:
परमेष्ठी परं ब्रह्म अक्षरं परमं पदम्।
श्रेष्ठस्त्वं वामदेवश्च रुद्रः स्कन्दः शिवः प्रभुः ॥ 55.32 ॥
1.55.m: You are the Supreme Lord, the supreme brahman, the imperishable, highest state. / You are the best, Vāmadeva, Rudra, Skanda, Śiva, the Sovereign.

1.55.s:
tvaṃ yajñastvaṃ vaṣaṭ‌kārastvamoṅkāraḥ paraṃ padam.
svāhākāro namaskāraḥ saṃskāraḥ sarvakarmaṇām .. 55.33 ..
1.55.d:
त्वं यज्ञस्त्वं वषट्‌कारस्त्वमोङ्कारः परं पदम्।
स्वाहाकारो नमस्कारः संस्कारः सर्वकर्मणाम् ॥ 55.33 ॥
1.55.m: You are the sacrifice, you are the vaṣaṭ-call, you are the syllable Oṃ, the highest state, / the svāhā-call, the salutation, the consecration of all rites;

1.55.s:
svadhākāraśca jāpyaśca vratāni niyamāstathā.
vedā lokāśca devāśca bhagavāneva sarvaśaḥ .. 55.34 ..
1.55.d:
स्वधाकारश्च जाप्यश्च व्रतानि नियमास्तथा।
वेदा लोकाश्च देवाश्च भगवानेव सर्वशः ॥ 55.34 ॥
1.55.m: the svadhā-call, recitation, religious observances, and restraints; / the Vedas, the worlds, and the gods—you alone are the Lord in all respects.

1.55.s:
ākāśasya ca śabdastvaṃ bhūtānāṃ prabhavāvyayam.
bhūmergandho rasaśvāpāṃ tejorūpaṃ maheśvara .. 55.35 ..
1.55.d:
आकाशस्य च शब्दस्त्वं भूतानां प्रभवाव्ययम्।
भूमेर्गन्धो रसश्वापां तेजोरूपं महेश्वर ॥ 55.35 ॥
1.55.m: You are the sound of space, the imperishable source of beings, / the fragrance of the earth, the taste of the waters, the form of fire, O Maheśvara;

1.55.s:
vāyoḥ ruparśaśca devaśca vapuścandramasastathā .
budho jñānañca deveśa prakṛtau bījameva ca .. 55.36 ..
1.55.d:
वायोः रुपर्शश्च देवश्च वपुश्चन्द्रमसस्तथा ।
बुधो ज्ञानञ्च देवेश प्रकृतौ बीजमेव च ॥ 55.36 ॥
1.55.m: the touch of wind, and the deity; likewise the form of the moon; / Budha and wisdom, O Lord of gods, and the seed within primal matter.

1.55.s:
tvaṃ karttā sarvabhūtānāṃ kālo mṛtyuryamo'ntakaḥ.
tvaṃ dhārayasi lokāstrīṃstvameva sṛjasi prabho .. 55.37 ..
1.55.d:
त्वं कर्त्ता सर्वभूतानां कालो मृत्युर्यमोऽन्तकः।
त्वं धारयसि लोकास्त्रींस्त्वमेव सृजसि प्रभो ॥ 55.37 ॥
1.55.m: You are the maker of all beings, Time, Death, Yama, the Ender; / you sustain the three worlds, you alone create them, O Lord!

1.55.s:
pūrveṇa vadanena tvamindratvañca prakāśase.
dakṣiṇena ca vakreṇa lokān saṃkṣīyase prabho .. 55.38 ..
1.55.d:
पूर्वेण वदनेन त्वमिन्द्रत्वञ्च प्रकाशसे।
दक्षिणेन च वक्रेण लोकान् संक्षीयसे प्रभो ॥ 55.38 ॥
1.55.m: With your eastern face you shine forth as Indra, / and with your southern face you destroy the worlds, O Lord.

1.55.s:
paścimena tu vakreṇa varuṇatvaṃ karoṣi vai.
uttareṇa tu vakreṇa saumyatvañca vyavasthitam .. 55.39 ..
1.55.d:
पश्चिमेन तु वक्रेण वरुणत्वं करोषि वै।
उत्तरेण तु वक्रेण सौम्यत्वञ्च व्यवस्थितम् ॥ 55.39 ॥
1.55.m: With your western face you act as Varuṇa, / and with your northern face benevolence is established.

1.55.s:
rājase bahudhā deva lokānāṃ prabhavāvyayaḥ.
ādityā vasavo rudrā marutaścāśvinīsutau .. 55.40 ..
1.55.d:
राजसे बहुधा देव लोकानां प्रभवाव्ययः।
आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा मरुतश्चाश्विनीसुतौ ॥ 55.40 ॥
1.55.m: You shine in many ways, O god, the imperishable origin of the worlds: / the ādityas, the vasus, the rudras, the maruts, the two sons of Aśvinī,

1.55.s:
sādhyā vidyādharā nāgāśvāraṇāśca tapodhanāḥ.
vālakhilyā mahātmānastapaḥ siddhāśca suvratāḥ .. 55.41 ..
1.55.d:
साध्या विद्याधरा नागाश्वारणाश्च तपोधनाः।
वालखिल्या महात्मानस्तपः सिद्धाश्च सुव्रताः ॥ 55.41 ॥
1.55.m: the sādhyas, the vidyādharas, the nāgas, the cāraṇas rich in austerities, / the great-souled vālakhilyas, perfected by asceticism and of good vows;

1.55.s:
tvattaḥ prasūtā deveśa ye cānye niyatavratāḥ.
umā sītā sinī vālī kuhūrgāyatrireva ca .. 55.42 ..
1.55.d:
त्वत्तः प्रसूता देवेश ये चान्ये नियतव्रताः।
उमा सीता सिनी वाली कुहूर्गायत्रिरेव च ॥ 55.42 ॥
1.55.m: from you are born, O Lord of gods, and whoever else of strict vows: / Umā, Sītā, Sinīvālī, Kuhū, and Gāyatrī;

1.55.s:
lakṣmīḥ kīrttirdhṛtirmedhā lajjā kṣāntirvapuḥ svadhā.
tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭhiḥ kriyā caiva vācāṃ devī sarasvatī.
tvattaḥ prasūtā deveśa sandhyā rātristathaiva ca .. 55.43 ..
1.55.d:
लक्ष्मीः कीर्त्तिर्धृतिर्मेधा लज्जा क्षान्तिर्वपुः स्वधा।
तुष्टिः पुष्ठिः क्रिया चैव वाचां देवी सरस्वती।
त्वत्तः प्रसूता देवेश सन्ध्या रात्रिस्तथैव च ॥ 55.43 ॥
1.55.m: Lakṣmī, Kīrti, Dhṛti, Medhā, Lajjā, Kṣānti, Vapuṣ, Svadhā, / Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Kriyā, and Sarasvatī, goddess of speech; / from you are born, O Lord of gods, twilight and night as well.

1.55.s:
sūryāyutānāmayutaprabhā ca namo'stu te candrasahasragocara.
namo'stu te parvatarūpadhāriṇe namo'stu te sarvaguṇākarāya .. 55.44 ..
1.55.d:
सूर्यायुतानामयुतप्रभा च नमोऽस्तु ते चन्द्रसहस्रगोचर।
नमोऽस्तु ते पर्वतरूपधारिणे नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वगुणाकराय ॥ 55.44 ॥
1.55.m: Homage be to you whose radiance equals tens of thousands of suns! Homage be to you who are visible as a thousand moons! / Homage be to you who bear the form of a mountain! Homage be to you, the mine of all virtues!

1.55.s:
namo'stu te paṭṭiśarūpadhāriṇe namo'stu te carmavibhūtidhāriṇe .
namo'stu te rudrapinākapāṇaye namo'stu te sāyakacakradhāriṇe .. 55.45 ..
1.55.d:
नमोऽस्तु ते पट्टिशरूपधारिणे नमोऽस्तु ते चर्मविभूतिधारिणे ।
नमोऽस्तु ते रुद्रपिनाकपाणये नमोऽस्तु ते सायकचक्रधारिणे ॥ 55.45 ॥
1.55.m: Homage be to you who bear the form of a paṭṭiśa! Homage be to you who bear an animal hide and ash! / Homage be to you, Rudra with Pināka in hand! Homage be to you who bear arrows and discus!

1.55.s:
namo'stu te bhasmavibhūṣitāṅga namo'stu te kāmaśarīranāśana.
namo'stu te deva hiraṇyavāsase namo'stu te deva hiraṇyabāhave .. 55.46 ..
1.55.d:
नमोऽस्तु ते भस्मविभूषिताङ्ग नमोऽस्तु ते कामशरीरनाशन।
नमोऽस्तु ते देव हिरण्यवाससे नमोऽस्तु ते देव हिरण्यबाहवे ॥ 55.46 ॥
1.55.m:
Homage be to you whose limbs are adorned with ashes! Homage be to you, destroyer of Kāma's body! / Homage be to you, O god clad in gold! Homage be to you, O god with golden arms!

Homage be to you, O god of golden form! Homage be to you, O god of golden navel! / Homage be to you, wonderful with a thousand eyes! Homage be to you, O god of golden seed!

1.55.s:
namo'stu te deva hiraṇyarūpa namo'stu te deva hiraṇyanābha.
namo'stu te netrasahasracitra namo'stu te deva hiraṇyaretaḥ .. 55.47 ..
1.55.d:
नमोऽस्तु ते देव हिरण्यरूप नमोऽस्तु ते देव हिरण्यनाभ।
नमोऽस्तु ते नेत्रसहस्रचित्र नमोऽस्तु ते देव हिरण्यरेतः ॥ 55.47 ॥
1.55.m:
Homage be to you, O god of golden complexion! Homage be to you, O god who are Hiraṇyagarbha! / Homage be to you, O god in golden bark-garments! Homage be to you, O god, giver of gold!

Homage be to you, O god wearing a golden garland! Homage be to you, O god with a golden chariot! / Homage be to you, O god in golden rags! Homage be to you who roar with a terrifying sound!

1.55.s:
namo'stu te deva hiraṇyavarṇa namo'stu te deva hiraṇyagarbha.
namo'stu te deva hiraṇyacīra namo'stu te deva hiraṇyadāyine .. 55.48 ..
1.55.d:
नमोऽस्तु ते देव हिरण्यवर्ण नमोऽस्तु ते देव हिरण्यगर्भ।
नमोऽस्तु ते देव हिरण्यचीर नमोऽस्तु ते देव हिरण्यदायिने ॥ 55.48 ॥

1.55.s:
namo'stu te deva hiraṇyamāline namo'stu te deva hiraṇyavāhine.
namo'stu te deva hiraṇyacīra namo'stu te bhairavanādanādine .. 55.49 ..
1.55.d:
नमोऽस्तु ते देव हिरण्यमालिने नमोऽस्तु ते देव हिरण्यवाहिने।
नमोऽस्तु ते देव हिरण्यचीर नमोऽस्तु ते भैरवनादनादिने ॥ 55.49 ॥
1.55.m: Homage be to you whose force is of terrible impetuosity! Homage be to you, Śaṅkara, blue-throated one! / Homage be to you with a thousand divine arms! Homage be to you who love dancing and musical instruments!

1.55.s:
namo'stu te bhairavavegavega namo'stu te śaṅkara nīlakaṇṭha.
mano'stu te divyasahasrabāho namo'stu te narttanavādanapriya .. 55.50 ..
1.55.d:
नमोऽस्तु ते भैरववेगवेग नमोऽस्तु ते शङ्कर नीलकण्ठ।
मनोऽस्तु ते दिव्यसहस्रबाहो नमोऽस्तु ते नर्त्तनवादनप्रिय ॥ 55.50 ॥

1.55.s:
evaṃ saṃstūyamānastu vyakto bhūtvā mahāmatiḥ.
bhāti devo mahāyogī sūryakoṭisamaprabhaḥ .. 55.51 ..
1.55.d:
एवं संस्तूयमानस्तु व्यक्तो भूत्वा महामतिः।
भाति देवो महायोगी सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभः ॥ 55.51 ॥
1.55.m: Thus being praised, the noble-minded god, the great yogin, / having become manifest, shone forth with the brilliance of ten million suns.

1.55.s:
abhibhāṣyastadā hṛṣṭo mahādevo maheśvaraḥ.
vakrakoṭisahasreṇa grasamāna ivāparam .. 55.52 ..
1.55.d:
अभिभाष्यस्तदा हृष्टो महादेवो महेश्वरः।
वक्रकोटिसहस्रेण ग्रसमान इवापरम् ॥ 55.52 ॥
1.55.m:
Then Mahādeva, the Great Lord, delighted, spoke [to them],
as though swallowing another [world] with ten million curved mouths.

1.55.s:
ekagrīvastvekajaṭo nānābhūṣaṇbhūṣitaḥ.
nānācitravicitrāṅgo nānāmālyānulepanaḥ .. 55.53 ..
1.55.d:
एकग्रीवस्त्वेकजटो नानाभूषण्भूषितः।
नानाचित्रविचित्राङ्गो नानामाल्यानुलेपनः ॥ 55.53 ॥
1.55.m:
Having a single neck, yet a single matted lock, adorned with various ornaments,
his limbs manifold and variegated, smeared with various unguents and garlands,

1.55.s:
pinākapāṇirbhagavān vṛṣabhāsanaśūladhṛk .
daṇḍakṛṣṇājinadharaḥ kapālī ghorarūpadhṛk .. 55.54 ..
1.55.d:
पिनाकपाणिर्भगवान् वृषभासनशूलधृक् ।
दण्डकृष्णाजिनधरः कपाली घोररूपधृक् ॥ 55.54 ॥
1.55.m:
the Lord holding the Pināka bow in hand, seated on a bull, bearer of the trident,
wearing a staff and black antelope skin, carrying a skull, bearing a terrible form,

1.55.s:
vyālayajñopavītī ca surāṇāmabhayaṅkaraḥ.
dundubhisvananirghoṣaparjanyaninadopamaḥ.
mukto hāsastadā tena nabhaḥ sarvamapūrayat .. 55.55 ..
1.55.d:
व्यालयज्ञोपवीती च सुराणामभयङ्करः।
दुन्दुभिस्वननिर्घोषपर्जन्यनिनदोपमः।
मुक्तो हासस्तदा तेन नभः सर्वमपूरयत् ॥ 55.55 ॥
1.55.m:
wearing a serpent as a sacred thread, granting fearlessness to the gods—
he then let out a laugh resembling the roar of a kettle-drum and thunderous rain-clouds,
which filled the entire sky.

1.55.s:
tena śabdena mahatā vayaṃ bhītā mahātmanaḥ.
tadovāca mahāyogī prīto'haṃ surasattamau .. 55.56 ..
1.55.d:
तेन शब्देन महता वयं भीता महात्मनः।
तदोवाच महायोगी प्रीतोऽहं सुरसत्तमौ ॥ 55.56 ॥
1.55.m:
At that tremendous sound we became terrified of the Great-souled One.
Then the great yogin said: 'I am pleased, O best of gods!

1.55.s:
paśyetāñca mahāmāyāṃ bhayaṃ sarvaṃ pramucyatām .
yuvāṃ prasūtau gātreṣu mama pūrvasanātanau .. 55.57 ..
1.55.d:
पश्येताञ्च महामायां भयं सर्वं प्रमुच्यताम् ।
युवां प्रसूतौ गात्रेषु मम पूर्वसनातनौ ॥ 55.57 ॥
1.55.m:
Behold the great illusory power (mahāmāyā); let all fear be cast away.
You two were born from my limbs, ancient and eternal.

1.55.s:
ayaṃ me dakṣiṇo bāhurbrahmā lokapitāmahaḥ.
vāmo bāhuśca me viṣṇurnityaṃ yuddheṣu tiṣṭhati.
prīto'haṃ yuvayoḥ samyagvaraṃ dajhi yathepsitam .. 55.58 ..
1.55.d:
अयं मे दक्षिणो बाहुर्ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः।
वामो बाहुश्च मे विष्णुर्नित्यं युद्धेषु तिष्ठति।
प्रीतोऽहं युवयोः सम्यग्वरं दझि यथेप्सितम् ॥ 55.58 ॥

1.55.s:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭamanasau praṇatau pādayoḥ punaḥ .
ūcatuśca mahātmānau punareva tadānaghau .. 55.59 ..
1.55.d:
ततः प्रहृष्टमनसौ प्रणतौ पादयोः पुनः ।
ऊचतुश्च महात्मानौ पुनरेव तदानघौ ॥ 55.59 ॥
1.55.m:
Then, their minds filled with joy, bowed at his feet again,
the two sinless, great-souled ones spoke once more:

1.55.s:
yadi prītiḥ samutpannā yadi deyo varaśca nau.
bhaktirbhavatu nau nityaṃ tvayi deva sureśvara .. 55.60 ..
1.55.d:
यदि प्रीतिः समुत्पन्ना यदि देयो वरश्च नौ।
भक्तिर्भवतु नौ नित्यं त्वयि देव सुरेश्वर ॥ 55.60 ॥
1.55.m:
'If pleasure has arisen [in you], and if a boon is to be given to us,
let there be constant devotion to you in us, O God, Lord of gods!'

1.55.s: ..bhagavānuvāca..
1.55.d: ॥भगवानुवाच॥
1.55.m:
The Lord said:
So be it, O illustrious ones; create diverse offspring.
Having spoken thus, the Lord vanished right there.

1.55.s:
evamastu mahābhāgau sṛjatāṃ vividhāḥ prajāḥ.
evamuktvā sa bhagavāṃstatraivāntaradhīyata .. 55.61 ..
1.55.d:
एवमस्तु महाभागौ सृजतां विविधाः प्रजाः।
एवमुक्त्वा स भगवांस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥ 55.61 ॥

1.55.s:
evameṣa mayokto vaḥ prabhāvastasya yoginaḥ.
tena sarvamidaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ hetumātrā vayantviha .. 55.62 ..
1.55.d:
एवमेष मयोक्तो वः प्रभावस्तस्य योगिनः।
तेन सर्वमिदं सृष्टं हेतुमात्रा वयन्त्विह ॥ 55.62 ॥
1.55.m:
Thus has this majesty of that yogin been related to you by me.
Everything here was created by him; we are merely instruments in this world.

1.55.s:
etaddhi rūpamajñātamavyaktaṃ śivasaṃjñitam.
acintyaṃ tadadṛśyañca paśyanti jñānacakṣuṣaḥ .. 55.63 ..
1.55.d:
एतद्धि रूपमज्ञातमव्यक्तं शिवसंज्ञितम्।
अचिन्त्यं तददृश्यञ्च पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः ॥ 55.63 ॥
1.55.m:
For this form is unknown, unmanifest, designated as Śiva;
inconceivable and invisible, those with the eye of knowledge behold it.

1.55.s:
tasmai devādhipatyāya namaskāraṃ prayuṅkta ha.
yena sūkṣmamacintyañca paśyanti jñānacakṣuṣaḥ .. 55.64 ..
1.55.d:
तस्मै देवाधिपत्याय नमस्कारं प्रयुङ्क्त ह।
येन सूक्ष्ममचिन्त्यञ्च पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः ॥ 55.64 ॥
1.55.m:
Pay obeisance unto that sovereign of the gods,
by whom [revealed], those with the eye of knowledge perceive the subtle and inconceivable.

1.55.s:
mahādeva namaste'stu maheśvara namo'stu te.
surāsuravara śreṣṭha manohaṃsa namo'stu te .. 55.65 ..
1.55.d:
महादेव नमस्तेऽस्तु महेश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते।
सुरासुरवर श्रेष्ठ मनोहंस नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 55.65 ॥
1.55.m:
Homage to you, O Mahādeva! Homage to you, O Maheśvara!
O supreme among gods and asuras, swan of the mind, homage to you!

1.55.s: ..sūta uvāca..
1.55.d: ॥सूत उवाच॥
1.55.m:
The Sūta said:
Having heard this, all the gods went each to his own dwelling,
offering homage to the great-souled Śaṅkara.

1.55.s:
etacchrutvā gatāḥ sarve surāḥ svaṃ svaṃ niveśanam.
namaskāraṃ prayuñjānāḥ śaṅkarāya mahātmane .. 55.66 ..
1.55.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा गताः सर्वे सुराः स्वं स्वं निवेशनम्।
नमस्कारं प्रयुञ्जानाः शङ्कराय महात्मने ॥ 55.66 ॥

1.55.s:
imaṃ stavaṃ paṭhedyastu īśvarasya mahātmanaḥ.
kāmāṃśca labhate sarvān pāpebhyastu vimucyate .. 55.67 ..
1.55.d:
इमं स्तवं पठेद्यस्तु ईश्वरस्य महात्मनः।
कामांश्च लभते सर्वान् पापेभ्यस्तु विमुच्यते ॥ 55.67 ॥
1.55.m:
Whoever recites this praise of the great-souled Īśvara
attains all desires and is freed from sins.

1.55.s:
etatsarvaṃ sadā tena viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā.
mahādevaprasādena uktaṃ brahma sanātanam.
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ mayā māheśvaraṃ balam .. 55.68 ..
1.55.d:
एतत्सर्वं सदा तेन विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना।
महादेवप्रसादेन उक्तं ब्रह्म सनातनम्।
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं मया माहेश्वरं बलम् ॥ 55.68 ॥
1.55.m:
All this was continually spoken by that all-powerful Viṣṇu
through the grace of Mahādeva as the eternal Brahman.
All this might of Maheśvara has been declared to you by me.

1.55.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte liṅgodbhavastavo nāma pañcapañcāśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 55 ..
1.55.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते लिङ्गोद्भवस्तवो नाम पञ्चपञ्चाशोऽध्यायः ॥ 55 ॥
1.55.m: Thus ends the fifty-fifth chapter, named 'Praise of the Origin of the Liṅga', in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.56.s: ..śāṃśapāyana uvāca ..
1.56.d: ॥शांशपायन उवाच ॥
1.56.m:
Śāṃśapāyana said:
How did the king, Aila Purūravas, go to heaven month after month
on the new-moon day, O Sūta, or how did he gratify the ancestors?

1.56.s:
agātkathamamāvāsyāṃ māsi māsi divaṃ nṛpaḥ.
ailaḥ purūravāḥ sūta kathaṃ vā'tarpayat pitṝn .. 56.1 ..
1.56.d:
अगात्कथममावास्यां मासि मासि दिवं नृपः।
ऐलः पुरूरवाः सूत कथं वाऽतर्पयत् पितॄन् ॥ 56.1 ॥

1.56.s: ..sūta uvāca..
1.56.d: ॥सूत उवाच॥
1.56.m:
The Sūta said:
And I shall declare to you, O Śāṃśapāyana, his power,
the conjunction of Aila with the sun, and of the great-souled Soma.

1.56.s:
tasya cāhaṃ pravakṣyāmi prabhāvaṃ śāṃśapāyana.
ailasyādityasaṃyogaṃ somasya ca mahātmanaḥ .. 56.2 ..
1.56.d:
तस्य चाहं प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रभावं शांशपायन।
ऐलस्यादित्यसंयोगं सोमस्य च महात्मनः ॥ 56.2 ॥

1.56.s:
apāṃsāramayasyendoḥ pakṣayoḥ śuklakṛṣṇayoḥ.
hrāsavṛddhī pitṛmataḥ pakṣasya ca vinirṇayaḥ .. 56.3 ..
1.56.d:
अपांसारमयस्येन्दोः पक्षयोः शुक्लकृष्णयोः।
ह्रासवृद्धी पितृमतः पक्षस्य च विनिर्णयः ॥ 56.3 ॥
1.56.m:
and the waning and waxing of the moon, which consists of the essence of the waters,
during the bright and dark fortnights, and the ascertainment of the fortnight regarding the ancestors;

1.56.s:
somāccaivāmṛtaprāptiḥ pitṝṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ tathā.
kavyāgneścāttasomānāṃ pitṝṇāñcaiva darśanam .. 56.4 ..
1.56.d:
सोमाच्चैवामृतप्राप्तिः पितॄणां तर्पणं तथा।
कव्याग्नेश्चात्तसोमानां पितॄणाञ्चैव दर्शनम् ॥ 56.4 ॥
1.56.m:
and the attainment of nectar from the moon, and likewise the propitiation of the ancestors;
and the vision of the ancestors who partake of soma from the fire of ancestral offerings (Kavyāgni);

1.56.s:
yathā purūravāścaila tarpayāmāsa vai pitṝn.
etatsarvaṃ pravakṣyāmi parvāṇi ca yathākramam .. 56.5 ..
1.56.d:
यथा पुरूरवाश्चैल तर्पयामास वै पितॄन्।
एतत्सर्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि पर्वाणि च यथाक्रमम् ॥ 56.5 ॥
1.56.m:
and how Purūravas Aila indeed satisfied the ancestors—
I shall declare all this, and the lunar days in proper order.

1.56.s:
yadā tu candrasūryau tau nakṣatreṇa samāgatau.
amāvāsyānnivasata ekarātraikamaṇḍale .. 56.6 ..
1.56.d:
यदा तु चन्द्रसूर्यौ तौ नक्षत्रेण समागतौ।
अमावास्यान्निवसत एकरात्रैकमण्डले ॥ 56.6 ॥
1.56.m:
When the sun and the moon are conjoined in a single asterism,
they dwell together for one night in a single orb on the new moon day.

1.56.s:
sa gacchati tadā draṣṭuṃ divākaraniśākarau.
amāvasyāmamāvāsyāṃ mātāmahapitāmahau.
abhivādya tadā tatra kālāpekṣaḥ pratīkṣyate .. 56.7 ..
1.56.d:
स गच्छति तदा द्रष्टुं दिवाकरनिशाकरौ।
अमावस्याममावास्यां मातामहपितामहौ।
अभिवाद्य तदा तत्र कालापेक्षः प्रतीक्ष्यते ॥ 56.7 ॥
1.56.m:
He then goes to see the sun and the moon
on each and every new moon day—his maternal grandfather and paternal grandfather.
Having greeted them there, he waits, awaiting the proper time.

1.56.s:
prasīdamānāt somācca pitrarthaṃ tatparisravāt.
ailaḥ purūravā vidvān māsi māsi prayatnataḥ.
uvāste pitṛmantaṃ taṃ sasomaṃ sa divāsthitaḥ .. 56.8 ..
1.56.d:
प्रसीदमानात् सोमाच्च पित्रर्थं तत्परिस्रवात्।
ऐलः पुरूरवा विद्वान् मासि मासि प्रयत्नतः।
उवास्ते पितृमन्तं तं ससोमं स दिवास्थितः ॥ 56.8 ॥
1.56.m:
From the moon being clarified and its overflowing exudation for the sake of the ancestors,
the wise Purūravas Aila, month after month, with diligence,
